definition_zh: 劳动；工作；劳动力；工党；分娩
definition_en: physical or mental work, especially hard work; also the workforce as a group and the process of giving birth
core_image: 两只手紧握工具，把力气一点点变成看得见的成果
scene: 天还没亮，工地上的灯已经亮起，工人们把沉重的沙袋一袋袋扛上肩。After a long day of labour, the crew sat down beside the unfinished wall.
sceneCN: 这里是「劳动、劳作」（第 1 个义项：付出体力的工作）；句意为干了一整天活之后，工人们坐在未完工的墙边歇下。图中可辨识物件：工地灯、沙袋、半截砖墙。

derivatives.zh: 由 labour 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「劳动者；工人」
由拉丁词干 labor 加 -ious 构成，义为「费力的；艰苦的」
由 labour 与 intensive 复合而成，义为「劳动密集型的」

senses.title: Physical work, especially of a hard kind
senses.definition: work, especially hard physical work, done with effort over time
senses.definitionCN: 尤指需要长时间付出体力的艰苦工作
senses.example: The wall was built through months of hard labour.
senses.exampleCN: 这堵墙是经过数月苦干才砌成的。
senses.why: Latin labor meant toil and hardship, so the word starts from the strain felt in the body rather than from the finished product.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 labor 本义是「辛劳、艰苦」，所以这个词的起点是身体感到的吃力，而不是最后完成的成果。

senses.title: The workforce as a group
senses.definition: the people who work, considered as a whole, especially in an industry or country
senses.definitionCN: 把从事工作的人作为一个整体来看，尤指某一行业或国家的劳动力
senses.example: The factory needs more skilled labour.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂需要更多技术工人。
senses.why: Once labour names the effort, it can also name the people who supply that effort, which is why the word shifts from activity to a collective body.
senses.whyCN: 既然 labour 能指付出的力气，也就能指提供这些力气的人，于是词义从「活动」转到「集体的人群」。

senses.title: Organized political labour
senses.titleCN: 工党；有组织的劳工运动
senses.definition: the political party or movement that represents the interests of workers
senses.definitionCN: 代表工人利益的政治党派或有组织的运动
senses.example: He voted for Labour in the last election.
senses.exampleCN: 上次选举他投了工党的票。
senses.why: When workers organize, the same word moves from the shop floor to the ballot box, naming the political force built on their shared interests.
senses.whyCN: 当工人联合起来，同一个词就从车间走向投票箱，用来指建立在他们共同利益之上的政治力量。

senses.title: Childbirth
senses.definition: the process of giving birth, especially the final stage with strong contractions
senses.definitionCN: 生育的过程，尤指伴随强烈宫缩的最后阶段
senses.example: She went into labour at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 她在黎明时开始分娩。
senses.why: Childbirth is the hardest bodily work a person can do, so English borrowed the word for toil to describe it, keeping the sense of intense physical effort.
senses.whyCN: 分娩是人身体上最吃力的一种劳作，英语便借「辛苦出力」这个词来描述它，保留了强烈体力付出的意味。

intro.en: Labour is a Latin word for toil that travelled through French before it named work, workers and birth in English.
intro.cn: labour 是拉丁语中表示「辛劳」的词，经法语进入英语，先指干活，再指劳动者与分娩。

items.en: Labor meant toil, hardship and effort, and it could also name the fruit of that effort.
items.cn: labor 意为辛劳、艰苦、出力，也可指付出之后得到的成果。

items.en: The verb laborare meant to work or to struggle, and it supplied the family of words about effort.
items.cn: 动词 laborare 意为干活、挣扎，派生出一整族与出力有关的词。

items.en: Old French took the noun as labour, meaning work or task, and passed it to English after the Norman conquest.
items.cn: 古法语把名词写作 labour，意为工作、活儿，诺曼征服之后传入英语。

items.en: Middle English labour covered both the act of working and the trouble or hardship that came with it.
items.cn: 中古英语的 labour 同时指干活这件事和随之而来的辛苦、磨难。

items.en: Modern English keeps the British spelling labour and the American labor, and extends the word to workers, their party and childbirth.
items.cn: 现代英语保留英式 labour 与美式 labor 两种拼写，并把词义扩展到劳动者、工党与分娩。

note.en: The look-alike group collects spellings and relatives built on the same Latin stem; the near-meaning group collects words for work and effort.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词干上的拼写与同族词；近义组收表示工作与出力的词。

entries.definition: The American spelling of labour, with the same meanings.
entries.definitionCN: labour 的美式拼写，含义完全相同。

entries.definition: Needing a lot of time and effort to do.
entries.definitionCN: 需要花费大量时间与力气的；费力的。

entries.definition: A room or building used for scientific work.
entries.definitionCN: 用于科学工作的房间或建筑；实验室。

entries.definition: To work together with someone on a task.
entries.definitionCN: 与某人合作完成一项任务。

entries.definition: Activity done to achieve a purpose, often as a job.
entries.definitionCN: 为达到目的而从事的活动，常指工作。

entries.definition: Long, hard and tiring work.
entries.definitionCN: 长时间、艰苦而累人的劳动。

entries.definition: The energy spent trying to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 为做某事而付出的精力。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on a Latin stem for toil, and its family keeps returning to effort, hardship and the people who do the work.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在表示「辛劳」的拉丁词干上，同族词反复回到出力、艰苦以及干活的人。

normal.en: Labor in Latin means toil, so labour is not just work but work that costs the body something.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 labor 意为辛劳，所以 labour 不只是工作，而是让身体付出代价的活。

normal.en: Labourer adds -er to labour: the person who does the labour.
normal.cn: labourer 在 labour 后加 -er，就是「干活的人」。

normal.en: Laborious adds -ious to the same stem: full of labour, therefore tiring.
normal.cn: laborious 在同一词干后加 -ious，意为「充满劳作的」，因此是费力的。

normal.en: The British spelling has a u, the American spelling drops it, just like colour and color.
normal.cn: 英式拼写带 u，美式去掉 u，就像 colour 与 color 一样。

normal.en: Labour Party is capitalized because it names a political party, not work in general.
normal.cn: Labour Party 首字母大写，因为它指一个政党，而不是泛指劳动。

abstract.en: A single word for effort, workers and birth suggests that English treats all three as kinds of hard work.
abstract.cn: 一个词同时表示出力、劳动者和分娩，说明英语把这三者都看成某种辛苦的劳作。

abstract.en: When a word moves from the body to the ballot box, the same strain is being organized into power.
abstract.cn: 当一个词从身体走向投票箱，同样的辛苦被组织成了力量。

abstract.en: Labour is a reminder that behind every finished thing there is a stretch of time that somebody had to endure.
abstract.cn: labour 提醒人：每件完成的东西背后，都有一段有人必须熬过去的时间。

examples.en: The wall was built through months of hard labour.
examples.cn: 这堵墙是经过数月苦干才砌成的。

examples.en: The country's labour force is growing older.
examples.cn: 这个国家的劳动力正在老龄化。

examples.en: She was in labour for six hours.
examples.cn: 她分娩持续了六个小时。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「累吧」——活儿干多了，人就会喊着累吧；记住 labour 是劳动。

root: 拉丁语 labor（劳作、辛苦）经古法语 labour 进入英语；同族词多与「干活、费力气」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is effortful work; the senses then divide into the people who work, their political party, and the hardest bodily work of all.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是费力的工作；义项由此分出干活的人、代表他们的政党，以及最吃力的身体劳作——分娩。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands gripping a tool and turning effort into a visible result.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手紧握工具，把力气一点点变成看得见的成果。

branches.en: a wall rising slowly under a hot sun
branches.cn: 烈日下一寸寸升起的墙

branches.en: a worker counting the hours until the shift ends
branches.cn: 工人数着还有多久下工

branches.en: a factory hiring more hands for the season
branches.cn: 工厂为旺季多招人手

branches.en: a ballot box standing in for the shop floor
branches.cn: 投票箱代替了车间

branches.en: a family waiting outside a delivery room
branches.cn: 产房外等候的一家人

intro.en: The word is held together by a Latin noun of toil, its verb, and two English suffixes that turn it into a person and a quality.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示辛劳的拉丁名词、它的动词，以及两个把它变成「人」和「性质」的英语后缀共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of

definition_zh: 缺乏；不足；缺少
definition_en: the state of not having something, or to be without something that is needed
core_image: 一只空碗摆在桌上，该有的东西一样也没盛上
scene: 厨房的储物柜被拉开，里面只剩几个空罐子。The cake failed because of a lack of flour.
sceneCN: 这里是「缺少、不足」（第 1 个义项：名词，指某物不存在或数量不够）；句意为蛋糕因为面粉不够而做失败了。图中可辨识物件：空罐子、空碗、打开的橱柜。

derivatives.zh: 由 lack 加 -ing 构成，义为「缺少的；不足的」
由 lack 与 luster（光泽）复合而成，义为「暗淡的；平淡无奇的」

senses.title: The state of not having enough of something
senses.definition: the state of not having something, or of not having enough of it
senses.definitionCN: 某物不存在或数量不够的状态
senses.example: The project was delayed by a lack of funds.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目因为资金不足而推迟。
senses.why: Lack names an empty place where something should be; the word points at the gap rather than at any object.
senses.whyCN: lack 指的是本该有东西却空着的位置，它指向的是那个缺口，而不是任何具体物件。

senses.title: To be without something needed
senses.definition: to have none of something, or not enough of it
senses.definitionCN: 完全没有某物，或某物的量不够
senses.example: Many students lack confidence in speaking English.
senses.exampleCN: 许多学生说英语时缺乏信心。
senses.why: The noun was turned into a verb without adding a suffix, so 'to lack' is simply to be in the state the noun names.
senses.whyCN: 名词原样转成动词，没有加后缀，所以 to lack 就是处在名词所指的那种「空着」的状态。

senses.title: A shortage that causes trouble
senses.definition: a shortage of something necessary, especially one that causes difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 必要之物短缺，尤指因此造成困难的情形
senses.example: The old town suffers from a lack of clean water.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老城饱受清洁水源短缺之苦。
senses.why: When the missing thing is necessary, the gap becomes a problem, and English extends lack from a neutral absence to a damaging shortage.
senses.whyCN: 当缺的是必需品时，那个缺口就成了麻烦，英语便从「中性的没有」扩展到「有害的短缺」。

intro.en: Lack is a Middle English word for a gap or deficiency, and its earlier source is not fully settled.
intro.cn: lack 是中古英语中表示「缺口、不足」的词，更早的来源尚无定论。

items.en: Lak meant a deficiency, fault or want, and it was used both as a noun and as a verb.
items.cn: lak 意为不足、缺陷、匮乏，名词与动词两种用法都有。

items.en: Many dictionaries suggest a Middle Dutch or Middle Low German source with the same sense, but the path is uncertain.
items.cn: 多数词典推测它来自意义相同的中古荷兰语或中古低地德语，但具体路径并不确定。

items.en: The word is recorded in English from the twelfth century onward, always close to the idea of something missing.
items.cn: 这个词从十二世纪起见于英语文献，始终贴近「有东西缺失」的概念。

items.en: Early modern writers use lack for both material shortage and personal fault, widening its range.
items.cn: 近代早期作家用 lack 兼指物资短缺与人的缺点，词义范围随之扩大。

items.en: Modern English keeps the simple noun and verb and builds phrases such as for lack of and lack of sleep.
items.cn: 现代英语保留名词与动词的基本用法，并形成 for lack of、lack of sleep 等搭配。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words sharing the spelling or the same stem; the near-meaning group gathers words for absence and shortage.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写相近或同词干的词；近义组收表示「没有、短缺」的词。

entries.definition: Missing or not having enough of something.
entries.definitionCN: 缺少的；不足的。

entries.definition: Dull and without energy or brightness.
entries.definitionCN: 暗淡的；平淡无奇的。

entries.definition: A servant who obeys orders without question.
entries.definitionCN: 唯命是从的仆人；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To fall behind or a delay.
entries.definitionCN: 落后；滞后；只是拼写相近。

entries.definition: A situation in which there is not enough of something.
entries.definitionCN: 短缺；不足。

entries.definition: The state of something not being present.
entries.definitionCN: 缺席；不存在。

entries.definition: A lack of something necessary.
entries.definitionCN: 缺乏；需要。

normalIntro.en: The word is short and blunt, and its few relatives all circle the idea of an empty place.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词短促直接，少数同族词都围绕「空着的位置」这一意思。

normal.en: Lack is both noun and verb with no change of shape: a lack of water, to lack water.
normal.cn: lack 名动同形：a lack of water 与 to lack water 都不加后缀。

normal.en: For lack of is a fixed phrase meaning 'because something is missing'.
normal.cn: for lack of 是固定搭配，意为「因为缺少某物」。

normal.en: Lacking adds -ing and works as an adjective: the lacking supplies.
normal.cn: lacking 加 -ing 作形容词：缺少的物资。

normal.en: Lackluster joins lack to luster, a word for shine.
normal.cn: lackluster 把 lack 与表示光泽的 luster 组合起来。

normal.en: The word never takes an article before the missing thing: lack of time, not lack of the time.
normal.cn: 说 lack of time，不说 lack of the time。

abstract.en: A word for a hole in a set of things reminds us that language can point at what is not there.
abstract.cn: 一个表示「一套东西里的空洞」的词，提醒人语言也能指向不在场的东西。

abstract.en: Because lack is neutral in shape, only context tells whether the gap is mild or dangerous.
abstract.cn: lack 本身是中性的，只有上下文才说明这个缺口是轻微还是危险。

abstract.en: Every shortage is measured against a standard that says how much should have been there.
abstract.cn: 每一种短缺都是对照「本该有多少」的标准量出来的。

examples.en: The cake failed because of a lack of flour.
examples.cn: 蛋糕因为面粉不够而做失败了。

examples.en: Many students lack confidence in speaking English.
examples.cn: 许多学生说英语时缺乏信心。

examples.en: There is no lack of volunteers for the event.
examples.cn: 这项活动的志愿者并不缺。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「来克」——东西没来够克数，就是缺；lack 记作「缺」。

root: 中古英语 lak（不足、缺陷），更早来源一般推测为中古荷兰语或中古低地德语，具体路径来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an empty place where something should be; the senses move from a neutral absence to a verb and then to a harmful shortage.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「本该有东西的空位」；义项从「中性的没有」转到动词用法，再转到「有害的短缺」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty bowl on a table where food should have been.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上摆着一只空碗，本该盛着食物。

branches.en: a pantry shelf with nothing on it
branches.cn: 空空如也的食品架

branches.en: a speaker searching for a word that will not come
branches.cn: 说话人找不到合适的词

branches.en: a village waiting for a water truck
branches.cn: 等水车来的村子

branches.en: the same gap, first seen and then suffered
branches.cn: 同一个缺口，先被看见，再让人吃苦

branches.en: a hand reaching for a tool that is not there
branches.cn: 伸手去拿却不存在的工具

intro.en: The word is a bare English stem with two common suffixes and one compound in its family.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个光裸的英语词干，同族里有两个常见后缀和一个复合词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaningCN: 构成形容词的 -ing 后缀
构成过去式的 -ed 后缀

definition_zh: 男孩；少年；小伙子；（英，非正式）哥们儿；马夫；农场小伙计
definition_en: a boy or young man, and in British informal use a male friend or workmate; also a dated word for a stable boy
core_image: 街角一个背着书包、吹着口哨跑过的少年
scene: 傍晚的街角，几个刚下班的年轻人靠在栏杆上聊天。A young lad in a paint-stained jacket told the others how his first day at work had gone.
sceneCN: 这里 lad 指「小伙子、年轻男孩」（第 1 个义项）；句意为一个外套沾着油漆的小伙子在讲他第一天上班的经历。图中可辨识物件：街角护栏、沾漆的外套、旧背包。

pos.zh: 男孩；少年；小伙子；哥们儿

derivatives.zh: 由 lad 加指小后缀 -ie 构成，多用于苏格兰英语，义为「小伙子；小家伙」
由 lad 加 -ish 构成，形容粗放、爱闹的年轻男性做派
由 lad 加女性后缀 -ette 构成，指举止像小伙子的年轻女性

senses.title: A boy or young man
senses.definition: a boy or young man, often one who is lively or comes from an ordinary working background
senses.definitionCN: 男孩或年轻男子，常指活泼或出身普通劳动阶层的年轻人
senses.example: A young lad was kicking a ball against the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 一个小伙子正对着墙踢球。
senses.why: Lad first named a male servant of low rank, so the word kept a plain, unpretentious tone when it widened to mean any boy or young man.
senses.whyCN: lad 最初指地位低下的男仆，因此当它扩大为泛指男孩、年轻人时，保留了朴素、不端架子的语气。

senses.title: A male friend or workmate
senses.definition: used in British informal speech for a man among friends, especially a workmate or teammate
senses.definitionCN: 英式口语中用来称呼朋友圈或工友、队友中的男性
senses.example: He went out for a drink with the lads from the warehouse.
senses.exampleCN: 他和仓库的哥们儿出去喝酒了。
senses.why: In a close group, a plain word for a male person turns into a badge of belonging: the lads are the men you work and drink with.
senses.whyCN: 在关系紧密的圈子里，一个指男性的朴素词会变成归属的标记：the lads 就是你一起干活、一起喝酒的那群人。

senses.title: A stable or farm boy
senses.definition: a boy or man who looks after horses or does farm work
senses.definitionCN: 照看马匹或干农活的男孩、男子
senses.example: The lad brushed down the horses before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 天还没亮，马夫就把马刷干净了。
senses.why: Before machines, farms and stables depended on young male helpers, so lad named the age and the job in one word.
senses.whyCN: 在机器出现之前，农场和马厩靠年轻的男性帮手，于是 lad 一个词同时指年龄和这份差事。

intro.en: Lad appears in Middle English as a word for a servant or a young man, and its further origin is not reliably known.
intro.cn: lad 在中古英语中出现，指仆役或年轻男子，更早的来源没有可靠结论。

items.en: The earliest records of lad, from about the thirteenth century, use it for a male servant or a man of low rank.
items.cn: lad 最早的记录大约出现在十三世纪，用来指男仆或地位低下的男子。

items.en: No reliable source has been established; ideas linking it to other languages remain guesses, and an unrecorded northern dialect form is only a suggestion.
items.cn: 它的来源至今没有可靠结论；把它与其他语言相联的想法都仍是猜测，所谓未被记录的北方方言形式也只是推测。

items.en: By the fourteenth century lad also meant simply a boy or a young man, and this everyday sense pushed the servant meaning into the background.
items.cn: 到十四世纪，lad 也已直接指男孩或年轻人，这个日常义项把「仆役」义推到幕后。

items.en: The word settled into ordinary speech and appeared in ballads and plays as a friendly or slightly rough way to name a young man.
items.cn: 这个词进入日常口语，在歌谣和戏剧里成为既亲切又略带粗气的「年轻人」称呼。

items.en: Modern British English keeps lad for a boy and for a mate, while laddie survives mainly in Scotland and laddish describes a style of male behaviour.
items.cn: 现代英式英语保留 lad 指男孩和伙伴；laddie 主要活在苏格兰，laddish 则形容一种男性做派。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on lad with familiar suffixes; the near-meaning group gathers other words for a young man or a male friend.
note.cn: 形近组收由 lad 加亲切后缀构成的词；近义组收其他表示年轻男子或男性伙伴的词。

entries.definition: A Scottish and affectionate word for a young lad.
entries.definitionCN: 苏格兰用语，亲切地指小伙子。

entries.definition: Behaving in the noisy, beer-and-football style associated with young men.
entries.definitionCN: 带有年轻人爱闹、喝酒看球那种做派的。

entries.definition: A young woman whose behaviour is modelled on laddish young men.
entries.definitionCN: 举止模仿粗放年轻男性的年轻女性。

entries.definition: A male child or a young male person.
entries.definitionCN: 男孩或年轻男性。

entries.definition: A young man, used especially in writing or older speech.
entries.definitionCN: 年轻人，多用于书面语或较早的说法。

entries.definition: A man, often used in a friendly or slightly old-fashioned way.
entries.definitionCN: 男人，常带亲切或略旧式的口吻。

entries.definition: A friend, especially a workmate or teammate.
entries.definitionCN: 朋友，尤指工友或队友。

normalIntro.en: The word began as a plain name for a low-ranking male servant and grew outward into boy, workmate and friend.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词最初是对低微男仆的朴素称呼，后来向外扩展到男孩、工友和朋友。

normal.en: Lad once meant a male servant, which is why it never sounds grand or formal.
normal.cn: lad 曾指男仆，所以它听起来从来不高贵、不正式。

normal.en: A young lad keeps the plainness and adds youth, the most common modern sense.
normal.cn: a young lad 保留那份朴素又加上年轻，是今天最常见的用法。

normal.en: The lads means the group you belong to, so the word turns friendship into a label.
normal.cn: the lads 指你所属的那群男性，于是这个词把友情变成了标签。

normal.en: Laddie adds a Scots diminutive -ie, making the same word warmer and smaller.
normal.cn: laddie 加上苏格兰指小后缀 -ie，让同一个词更亲昵、更小。

normal.en: Laddish and ladette build on lad to describe a style of behaviour, not a person's age.
normal.cn: laddish 与 ladette 都在 lad 上构词，描述一种行为风格，而不是年龄。

abstract.en: A word can start at the bottom of a household and end up as a friendly shout across a street.
abstract.cn: 一个词可以从家庭最底层的位置出发，最后变成街对面一声亲切的招呼。

abstract.en: The same syllable names a boy, a worker and a friend, because all three are the same person seen from different distances.
abstract.cn: 同一个音节指男孩、工人和朋友，因为三者只是从不同距离看同一个人。

abstract.en: Lad is a reminder that English often keeps its warmest words for the plainest people.
abstract.cn: lad 提醒人：英语常把最温暖的词留给最普通的人。

examples.en: A young lad was kicking a ball against the wall.
examples.cn: 一个小伙子正对着墙踢球。

examples.en: He went out for a drink with the lads from the warehouse.
examples.cn: 他和仓库的哥们儿出去喝酒了。

examples.en: The lad brushed down the horses before dawn.
examples.cn: 天还没亮，马夫就把马刷干净了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「来的」——街角跑来的那个小伙子；记住 lad 是少年、小伙子。

root: 来源不确定；一般认为出现于十三世纪的中古英语，最初指男仆或地位低下的男子，后泛指男孩与年轻人。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a young male of plain background; the word then splits into the working boy, the friend in a group, and the boy who tends horses.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是出身普通的年轻男性；词义随后分出干活的男孩、圈子里的伙伴，以及照看马匹的小伙计。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lanky boy in a worn jacket running past a street corner.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个穿着旧外套、瘦高的男孩从街角跑过。

branches.en: a boy kicking a ball against a brick wall
branches.cn: 一个男孩对着砖墙踢球

branches.en: a young helper starting his first shift on a farm
branches.cn: 一个年轻帮工在农场开始第一班活

branches.en: a stable boy brushing horses before sunrise
branches.cn: 天不亮就刷马的马夫

branches.en: friends sharing a drink after work
branches.cn: 下班后一起喝酒的朋友

branches.en: a rough but warm shout across the street
branches.cn: 街对面一声粗粝却温暖的招呼

intro.en: The word is a bare Middle English noun, and English suffixes build its family outward into pet form, manner and female counterpart.
intro.cn: 这个词是光秃秃的中古英语名词，英语后缀把它的词族向外扩展成昵称、做派与女性对应形式。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: an affectionate word for a lad
behaving like a rowdy young man
a young woman with laddish behaviour

definition_zh: 梯子；阶梯；晋升阶梯；（长袜的）抽丝
definition_en: a frame with rungs used for climbing; also a graded series of levels, a run in a stocking, or to climb by means of a ladder
core_image: 靠在墙边的木梯，一级一级通向高处
scene: 仓库的屋顶坏了一块，师傅把梯子靠在墙边，仰头看了看上面的缺口。He climbed the ladder to fix the roof tiles before the rain came.
sceneCN: 这里是「梯子」（第 1 个义项：供人攀爬的用具）；句意是他在下雨前爬上梯子修屋顶的瓦片。图中可辨识物件：木梯、砖墙、屋顶缺口。

pos.zh: 用梯子攀爬；使织物抽丝

derivatives.zh: 由 ladder 加 -ed 构成，义为「有梯级的；抽丝的」
由 ladder 加 -ing 构成，义为「织物抽丝；阶梯式安排」
由 ladder 与 like 复合而成，义为「梯状的」

senses.title: A frame used for climbing
senses.definition: a set of steps or rungs joined by two side pieces, used to reach high places
senses.definitionCN: 由两侧支柱连接若干横档组成、用来够到高处的攀爬用具
senses.example: The painter left the ladder against the wall overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 油漆工把梯子靠在墙边过了一夜。
senses.why: Old English hlæder named a leaning frame, and that concrete object is still the first sense anyone pictures.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 hlæder 指可以斜靠的架子，所以这个具体物件仍是人们最先想到的义项。

senses.title: A graded series of levels
senses.definition: a sequence of ranks or stages that someone moves through, especially in a career
senses.definitionCN: 某人依次经历的一串等级或阶段，尤指职业上的晋升
senses.example: She worked her way up the corporate ladder one promotion at a time.
senses.exampleCN: 她沿着企业晋升阶梯，一步一步往上走。
senses.why: A real ladder is climbed rung by rung, so the same picture is borrowed for any ranked order that is advanced one stage at a time.
senses.whyCN: 真正的梯子要一级一级往上爬，于是同一幅画面被借来形容任何逐级上升的等级序列。

senses.title: A run in stockings or tights
senses.definition: a long tear in a stocking or pair of tights that spreads in a line
senses.definitionCN: 长袜或连裤袜上沿一条线延伸的裂口
senses.example: A ladder in her tights forced her to change before the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 长袜上的一处抽丝让她不得不在开会前换掉。
senses.why: The thin line of a run looks like a row of rungs running down the fabric, which is why British English calls it a ladder.
senses.whyCN: 抽丝形成的那道细线像一排横档顺着织物往下走，英式英语因此把它叫作 ladder。

senses.title: To climb with or as if with a ladder
senses.titleCN: 用梯子攀爬；借助梯状物攀升
senses.definition: to climb or reach something using a ladder, or to move up as if using one
senses.definitionCN: 借助梯子爬向或够到某处，也指像踩梯子一样向上移动
senses.example: The rescue team laddered the cliff and reached the stranded hikers.
senses.exampleCN: 救援队借助梯状绳索攀上崖壁，到达被困的徒步者身边。
senses.why: The noun came first; turning it into a verb simply adds the action of using the object, in the same way that brush became to brush.
senses.whyCN: 名词先出现，把它用作动词只是补上「使用这个物件」的动作，就像 brush 变成 to brush 一样。

intro.en: Ladder is an old Germanic word with no Latin ancestor; English has carried it from a leaning frame to ranked levels and torn stockings.
intro.cn: ladder 是古老的日耳曼语词，没有拉丁语祖先；英语把它从斜靠的架子一路用到等级阶梯和长袜抽丝。

items.en: A distant root is sometimes suggested, but the reconstruction is uncertain and should not be treated as settled.
items.cn: 有时会提出一个更古老的远祖词根，但该重构并不确定，不宜当作定论。

items.en: The Germanic form is reconstructed as hlaidrijō, naming something that leans or is propped up.
items.cn: 日耳曼语形式常重构为 hlaidrijō，指可以倚靠或支撑起来的东西。

items.en: Old English hlæder already meant a ladder, and the word appears in texts about building and farming.
items.cn: 古英语 hlæder 已指梯子，这个词见于建筑与农事文本。

items.en: Middle English smoothed the consonant cluster and wrote ladder, the spelling English still uses.
items.cn: 中古英语简化了辅音组合，写作 ladder，也就是今天沿用的拼写。

items.en: Modern English extended the noun to ranks and to a run in fabric, and turned it into a verb of climbing.
items.cn: 现代英语把名词扩展到等级和织物抽丝，并派生出表示攀爬的动词。

note.en: The look-alike group collects compounds and suffixes built on ladder; the near-meaning group collects things climbed or stepped on.
note.cn: 形近组收由 ladder 构成的复合词与加缀词；近义组收供人攀爬、踩踏的同类事物。

entries.definition: A folding ladder with steps instead of plain rungs.
entries.definitionCN: 一种带踏步而非普通横档的折叠梯；梯凳。

entries.definition: Marked with a run, or fitted with rungs.
entries.definitionCN: 有抽丝的；装有横档的。

entries.definition: The forming of a run in tights, or the arranging of levels.
entries.definitionCN: 长袜抽丝；阶梯式的层级安排。

entries.definition: The second of two things mentioned; only the spelling is close, since the history of the word is different.
entries.definitionCN: 两者中的后者；只是拼写相近，词源并不相同。

entries.definition: A set of steps built into a building for going up and down.
entries.definitionCN: 建筑物内固定安装、供上下行走的一段楼梯。

entries.definition: The whole structure of stairs, including its frame and handrail.
entries.definitionCN: 楼梯的整体结构，包括框架与扶手。

entries.definition: One of the crossbars that form the steps of a ladder.
entries.definitionCN: 梯子上构成踏步的一根横档。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Germanic simplex noun, and its compounds and suffixes move it from a climbing tool to rank and to torn fabric.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是日耳曼语的单纯名词，复合词与后缀把它从攀爬工具延伸到等级和抽丝的织物。

normal.en: Old English hlæder became ladder by smoothing the consonant cluster, so the modern form is a shortened, easier mouthful.
normal.cn: 古英语 hlæder 经过辅音简化变成 ladder，所以现代拼写是更省力的一串音。

normal.en: Ladder belongs to the Germanic layer of English, not to the Latin layer, so it has no Latin relative to learn with it.
normal.cn: ladder 属于英语的日耳曼语层，而不是拉丁语层，所以不必为它硬找拉丁同族词。

normal.en: Stepladder is simply step plus ladder: a ladder whose steps are broad boards rather than thin rungs.
normal.cn: stepladder 就是 step 加 ladder：踏板是宽板而不是细横档的梯子。

normal.en: Rung is the name of a single crossbar, which is why climbing a ladder means moving from rung to rung.
normal.cn: rung 是单根横档的名字，所以爬梯子就是一级横档一级横档地移动。

normal.en: The corporate ladder keeps the climbing picture and turns each promotion into one more rung.
normal.cn: corporate ladder 保留了攀爬的画面，把每一次晋升都变成又一级横档。

abstract.en: A tool that exists only to raise a person explains why the word so easily becomes a picture of ambition.
abstract.cn: 一种只为把人送高的工具，解释了为什么这个词很容易变成野心的图画。

abstract.en: The same thin line that marks a climb also marks a tear, so ascent and damage share one shape.
abstract.cn: 标记攀爬的那道细线也能标记裂口，于是上升与破损共用了同一种形状。

abstract.en: Ladder reminds us that height is reached in small, repeated moves rather than in one leap.
abstract.cn: ladder 提醒人：高度是靠一次次小移动到达的，而不是一步跃上去的。

examples.en: The painter left the ladder against the wall overnight.
examples.cn: 油漆工把梯子靠在墙边过了一夜。

examples.en: She worked her way up the corporate ladder one promotion at a time.
examples.cn: 她沿着企业晋升阶梯，一步一步往上走。

examples.en: A ladder in her tights forced her to change before the meeting.
examples.cn: 长袜上的一处抽丝让她不得不在开会前换掉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「累的」——爬梯子爬到腿都累了；记住 ladder 是梯子。

root: 古英语 hlæder，属日耳曼语固有词；一般认为与表示「倾斜、倚靠」的词有远亲关系，与拉丁语没有直接同源关系。

sensesIntro.en: The concrete climbing frame is the core; from it come the ranked ladder of promotion, the ladder-like run in fabric, and the verb of climbing.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是具体的攀爬架子；由此分出表示晋升的等级阶梯、织物上梯状的抽丝，以及表示攀爬的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wooden ladder leaning against a wall, its rungs leading upward.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把木梯靠在墙边，横档一级级通向高处。

branches.en: a wooden frame leaning against a wall
branches.cn: 靠在墙边的一架木梯

branches.en: hands moving from rung to rung in the dark
branches.cn: 黑暗中双手一级一级向上移动

branches.en: a chart where each box is a promotion
branches.cn: 每一格代表一次晋升的图表

branches.en: a climb that never seems to end
branches.cn: 一场仿佛没有尽头的攀升

branches.en: a thin line running down a stocking
branches.cn: 长袜上向下延伸的一道细线

intro.en: A Germanic noun is extended by one compound with step and by two suffixes that produce an adjective and a noun.
intro.cn: 这个日耳曼语名词由 step 构成的复合词，以及两个分别造出形容词和名词的后缀来扩展。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: a frame with rungs for climbing
one rung or a movement of the foot
marked with a run or with rungs
the forming of a run in fabric

definition_zh: 女士；贵妇人；夫人（头衔）；女主人
definition_en: a polite word for a woman; also a woman of high social rank, a title before a name, or the woman who runs a household
core_image: 宴会上一位女士端着茶盏，满座宾客起身让路
scene: 宴会上灯光明亮，主人起身迎向门口的客人。Every gentleman stood up when the lady entered the room.
sceneCN: 这里是「女士」（第 1 个义项：对成年女性的礼貌称呼）；句意为这位女士走进房间时，每位先生都站了起来。可辨识画面：宴席、起身的宾客、门口的身影。

pos.zh: 女士；贵妇人；夫人；女主人

derivatives.zh: 由 lady 加后缀 -like（像……的）构成，义为「举止像贵妇的；优雅的」
由 lady 加 -ship（身份、地位）构成，用于尊称贵族妇女「夫人」
由 land 与 lady 复合，指出租房屋或经营客栈的女主人，义为「女房东」

senses.title: A polite word for a woman
senses.titleCN: 女士；对女性的礼貌称呼
senses.definition: a polite way of referring to or addressing an adult woman
senses.definitionCN: 礼貌地指称或称呼一位成年女性
senses.example: The lady at the front desk helped me find my room.
senses.exampleCN: 前台那位女士帮我找到了房间。
senses.why: The Old English word named the woman who ran the household, and courtesy kept it as a respectful label for any adult woman.
senses.whyCN: 古英语这个词原本指掌管一家的女主人，礼貌用法把它保留为对任何成年女性的尊称。

senses.title: The mistress of a household
senses.definition: the woman who owns or runs a house or an establishment
senses.definitionCN: 拥有或掌管一个家、一处场所的女性
senses.example: She was the lady of the house and everyone answered to her.
senses.exampleCN: 她是这家的女主人，人人都听她安排。
senses.why: Because the old compound meant the woman in charge of the bread, the authority inside a home survived as a meaning of its own.
senses.whyCN: 原词本指负责烤面包的女人，掌管一家的意味就作为独立义项留存了下来。

senses.title: A title placed before a name
senses.definition: the title used before the name of a woman of noble rank
senses.definitionCN: 用在贵族女性姓名之前的尊称
senses.example: Lady Mary opened the charity fair.
senses.exampleCN: 玛丽夫人为慈善集市揭幕。
senses.why: A title is a fossil of rank: the old word for a noble housewife became the fixed label for titled women.
senses.whyCN: 头衔是等级的化石：原本指贵族家女主人的词，固定成了贵族女性的称谓。

senses.title: A woman hired for a particular job
senses.definition: a woman employed to do a particular job, as in cleaning lady
senses.definitionCN: 受雇从事某项工作的女性，如保洁女工
senses.example: The cleaning lady comes every Friday morning.
senses.exampleCN: 保洁女工每周五上午来。
senses.why: When the word is attached to a job name, the old polite label simply marks that the worker is a woman.
senses.whyCN: 当它跟在职业名称后面时，这个旧的礼貌称呼只用来标明干这份活的是女性。

intro.en: Lady goes back to an Old English compound that literally meant bread-kneader, the woman who fed and therefore ran the household.
intro.cn: lady 可追到一个古英语复合词，字面意为「揉面包的人」，即养活全家、因而管着全家的女人。

items.en: Hlāf meant bread, the same Germanic word that became loaf in modern English.
items.cn: hlāf 意为面包，与今天的 loaf 同出一个日耳曼词。

items.en: Dīge meant a kneader or maker of dough, formed from a verb for kneading.
items.cn: dīge 意为揉面者、做面团的人，由表示揉面的动词构成。

items.en: Put together, hlǣfdige was the bread-kneader, the woman who fed the household and therefore ran it.
items.cn: 两者合成 hlǣfdige，本指揉面做面包的女人，她养活全家，也就管着全家。

items.en: Middle English shortened and softened the long compound into lady, already applied to noblewomen and to the Virgin Mary.
items.cn: 中古英语把这个长复合词缩短、软化，写作 lady，已用来指贵族女性与圣母。

items.en: Modern English uses lady as a polite term, a noble title and a word for women in particular jobs.
items.cn: 现代英语把 lady 用作礼貌称呼、贵族头衔，以及指从事特定工作的女性。

note.en: The look-alike group collects compounds and words that share the spelling or the lady element; the near-meaning group collects words for women and forms of address.
note.cn: 形近组收共用拼写或共用 lady 这一成分的复合词；近义组收表示女性与称呼的用词。

entries.definition: A small flying beetle with red or orange spotted wings.
entries.definitionCN: 一种红色或橙色带斑点的会飞的小甲虫；构词里用了 lady。

entries.definition: Behaving in a quiet, graceful way thought to suit a lady.
entries.definitionCN: 举止安静优雅、被认为合乎贵妇身份的。

entries.definition: A deep spoon with a long handle, used for serving soup.
entries.definitionCN: 舀汤用的长柄深勺；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A set of steps used for climbing up or down.
entries.definitionCN: 供上下攀爬的一串梯级；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: An adult female person, the plain word that lady politely replaces.
entries.definitionCN: 成年女性；lady 是对它的一种礼貌替代。

entries.definition: A polite form used to address a woman, especially a customer.
entries.definitionCN: 称呼女性的礼貌用语，尤用于顾客。

entries.definition: A polite word for a man, the male counterpart of lady.
entries.definitionCN: 对男性的礼貌称呼，与 lady 相对。

entries.definition: A title used before the name of an unmarried woman or girl.
entries.definitionCN: 用于未婚女性或女孩姓名前的称谓。

normalIntro.en: The word was built from bread and kneading, and its family keeps returning to the household, the title and the polite label.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由「面包」与「揉面」合成，同族词反复回到家庭、头衔与礼貌称呼。

normal.en: Hlāf is bread and dīge is kneader, so a lady was first the woman who kneaded bread for the household.
normal.cn: hlāf 是面包，dīge 是揉面的人，所以 lady 最初指为全家揉面做面包的女人。

normal.en: The long form hlǣfdige explains why lady shows no trace of bread today: the compound was worn down over centuries.
normal.cn: 古英语长词 hlǣfdige 说明今天看不出「面包」的原因：这个词组在几百年里被磨损缩短了。

normal.en: Lady has the plural ladies, because a y after a consonant turns into ies.
normal.cn: lady 的复数是 ladies，因为辅音后的 y 要变成 ies。

normal.en: Ladybird is a compound: a small beetle named after Our Lady, not a bird at all.
normal.cn: ladybird 是复合词：这种小甲虫的名字来自圣母，其实根本不是鸟。

normal.en: Ladies and gentlemen is a fixed order, so the ladies always come first in that phrase.
normal.cn: ladies and gentlemen 是固定顺序，短语里女士总排在前面。

abstract.en: A word that began with bread suggests that rank in a household was first measured by who fed it.
abstract.cn: 一个从面包开始的词说明，家里的地位最初是按谁来养活全家来衡量的。

abstract.en: Lady survives as politeness, which shows how a job title can soften into a form of respect.
abstract.cn: lady 作为礼貌用语活了下来，说明一个职务称呼可以软化成一种敬意。

abstract.en: Calling someone a lady is a small gift of dignity, so the word carries courtesy rather than description.
abstract.cn: 称某人为 lady 是送出一份体面，所以这个词带的是礼貌而不是描述。

examples.en: The lady at the front desk helped me find my room.
examples.cn: 前台那位女士帮我找到了房间。

examples.en: A young lady asked me for directions.
examples.cn: 一位年轻女士向我问路。

examples.en: The cleaning lady comes every Friday morning.
examples.cn: 保洁女工每周五上午来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「累地」——她踩着高跟鞋走了一整天，累得只想找块地坐下；记住 lady 是女士。

root: 古英语 hlǣfdige，由 hlāf（面包）与 dīge（揉面者）合成，本指做面包的女主人，后来泛指女士与贵妇。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a woman in charge of a household; the senses then spread to a general polite term, a noble title and women in particular jobs.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是掌管一家的女性；义项由此扩展到泛指的礼貌称呼、贵族头衔以及从事特定工作的女性。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a woman holding a fresh loaf while the household gathers around her.
core.cn: 核心意象：一位妇人手里捧着刚出炉的面包，全家围着她转。

branches.en: a woman greeting guests at a bright banquet
branches.cn: 宴会上向宾客致意的女士

branches.en: a housewife handing out the day's bread
branches.cn: 女主人分派当天的面包

branches.en: a titled name printed on an invitation
branches.cn: 请柬上印着的贵族头衔

branches.en: a worker mopping the office floor at dawn
branches.cn: 清晨在办公室拖地的女工

branches.en: a photograph of a woman standing in a doorway
branches.cn: 一张妇人站在门口的照片

intro.en: Old English bread, the old word for a kneader, and two modern suffixes all meet in this word.
intro.cn: 古英语的「面包」、表示揉面者的旧词，以及两个现代后缀，都汇聚在这个词里。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic in origin and has no reliable Latin cognate.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词源自日耳曼语，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

items.meaning: lady plus bird, a small spotted beetle
items.meaningCN: lady 与 bird 复合，指带斑点的甲虫

items.meaning: land plus lady, a woman who owns a rented house
items.meaningCN: land 与 lady 复合，指出租房屋的女主人

definition_zh: 落后；滞后；时间间隔
definition_en: to fall behind others in movement or progress, or a delay between two events
core_image: 队伍前面的人已转过弯，最后一个还在原地系鞋带
scene: 操场上的队伍已经跑出半圈，最后一名选手才刚系好鞋带。The oldest computer began to lag behind the others.
sceneCN: 这里是「落后、跟不上」（第 1 个义项：动词，指行动或进度落在别人后面）；句意为最旧的电脑开始落在其他电脑后面。图中可辨识物件：跑道、系鞋带的选手、远处的队伍。

derivatives.zh: 由 lag 双写 g 加 -ing 构成，义为「落后的；滞后」
由 lag 加 -ard 构成，义为「迟缓的人；落后者」

senses.title: To fall behind in movement or progress
senses.definition: to move or develop more slowly than others, so that a distance opens up
senses.definitionCN: 行动或发展比其他人慢，因而拉开距离
senses.example: The oldest computer began to lag behind the others.
senses.exampleCN: 最旧的电脑开始落在其他电脑后面。
senses.why: Lag probably imitates the sense of something dragging at the back; the word pictures a trailing end rather than a measured distance.
senses.whyCN: lag 很可能来自「拖在后面」的感觉，它描绘的是队尾，而不是量出来的距离。

senses.title: A delay between two connected events
senses.definition: the period of time by which one event follows another that should be simultaneous
senses.definitionCN: 两个本应同时的事件之间相隔的那段时间
senses.example: There is a slight time lag between the sound and the picture.
senses.exampleCN: 声音和画面之间有一点时间滞后。
senses.why: Once the verb names being behind, the noun can name the measurable gap itself, as in a time lag.
senses.whyCN: 动词既然表示「落在后面」，名词就能指那段可测量的差距，例如 time lag。

senses.title: The tiredness caused by crossing time zones
senses.definition: the bodily discomfort felt after a long flight across several time zones
senses.definitionCN: 跨越多个时区长途飞行后身体感到的不适
senses.example: It took him three days to get over his jet lag.
senses.exampleCN: 他花了三天才缓过时差反应。
senses.why: The body's internal clock lags behind local time after a flight, and the compound jet lag names exactly that lag.
senses.whyCN: 飞行之后，身体的生物钟落后于当地时间，jet lag 这个复合词正是把这种「滞后」说了出来。

intro.en: Lag is a word of uncertain origin, usually connected with Scandinavian forms for something dragging behind.
intro.cn: lag 来源不确定，通常与斯堪的纳维亚语中表示「拖在后面」的形式相联系。

items.en: The earliest records do not settle whether lag came from Scandinavian or from an English dialect.
items.cn: 最早记录无法确定 lag 是来自斯堪的纳维亚语还是英格兰方言。

items.en: A related Swedish dialect verb for moving slowly or dragging is often cited, but the exact form is uncertain.
items.cn: 常被提到的是一个意义为「慢慢移动、拖」的瑞典方言动词，但确切形式并不确定。

items.en: Lag appears in English in the sixteenth century with the sense of trailing behind.
items.cn: lag 在十六世纪进入英语，意为「拖在后面」。

items.en: The noun and the modern technical sense of a time lag develop in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 名词用法以及 time lag 这一现代技术义在十九世纪发展出来。

items.en: Modern English adds jet lag and digital lag, keeping the same picture of something running behind.
items.cn: 现代英语又添上 jet lag 与 digital lag，仍保留「某物跑在后面」的画面。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that resemble lag in spelling; the near-meaning group collects words for delay and trailing behind.
note.cn: 形近组收与 lag 拼写相近的词；近义组收表示延迟、落后的词。

entries.definition: A piece of cloth used as a signal, or to become tired.
entries.definitionCN: 旗子；也可指「变得疲倦」；只是拼写相近。

entries.definition: A small label attached to something.
entries.definitionCN: 标签；只是拼写相近。

entries.definition: Falling behind, or material used for insulation.
entries.definitionCN: 落后的；保温材料。

entries.definition: A period of waiting before something happens.
entries.definitionCN: 延迟；耽搁。

entries.definition: To be behind others in a race or competition.
entries.definitionCN: 落后；尾随。

entries.definition: A reduction in speed or activity.
entries.definitionCN: 减速；放慢。

normalIntro.en: The word is short, with a doubled g in its inflections, and its family stays close to the trailing end of a line.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词很短，变形时双写 g，同族词都贴近队伍末尾。

normal.en: Lag doubles its g before -ed and -ing: lagged, lagging.
normal.cn: lag 在 -ed、-ing 前双写 g：lagged、lagging。

normal.en: Lag behind is the common phrase for being slower than others.
normal.cn: lag behind 是表示「落在别人后面」的常用搭配。

normal.en: Time lag is the measurable gap between two events.
normal.cn: time lag 是两个事件之间可测量的间隔。

normal.en: Jet lag joins jet to lag for the tiredness after a flight.
normal.cn: jet lag 把 jet 与 lag 组合，指飞行后的疲倦。

normal.en: Laggard adds -ard, a suffix seen in words for people with a habit.
normal.cn: laggard 加 -ard，这个后缀常见于表示有某种习性的人。

abstract.en: A trailing end is not a fixed distance but a relation: someone must be ahead for lag to exist.
abstract.cn: 队尾不是固定距离而是一种关系：必须有人在前面，才有 lag。

abstract.en: The same word covers a runner, a machine and a body clock, because all three can run behind an expected pace.
abstract.cn: 同一个词能指跑步的人、机器和生物钟，因为三者都可能落后于预期节奏。

abstract.en: Lag turns difference in speed into something you can name and measure.
abstract.cn: lag 把速度上的差异变成可以命名、可以测量的东西。

examples.en: The oldest computer began to lag behind the others.
examples.cn: 最旧的电脑开始落在其他电脑后面。

examples.en: There is a slight time lag between the sound and the picture.
examples.cn: 声音和画面之间有一点时间滞后。

examples.en: It took him three days to get over his jet lag.
examples.cn: 他花了三天才缓过时差反应。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「赖格」——赖在格子里不肯往前走，就落后了；lag 记作「落后」。

root: 来源不确定，一般认为与斯堪的纳维亚语中表示「拖在后面」的方言动词有关，确切形式无法确认。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a trailing end; it extends from a person falling behind to a measurable time gap and to the body clock running late.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「拖在队尾」；由人落后扩展到可测量的时间差，再扩展到生物钟的错后。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the last runner still tying a shoelace while the line turns the corner.
core.cn: 核心意象：队伍已经转过弯，最后一名还在系鞋带。

branches.en: a runner at the back of the pack
branches.cn: 跑在队伍最后的人

branches.en: a clock that is a few seconds slow
branches.cn: 慢了几秒的钟

branches.en: a traveller awake at the wrong hour
branches.cn: 在错误时间醒来的旅客

branches.en: the same backward pull, in legs and in seconds
branches.cn: 同一种向后拖的力量，表现在腿上和秒数上

branches.en: two screens showing the same scene a beat apart
branches.cn: 两块屏幕同一画面差了一拍

intro.en: There is no settled prefix or root here, so the family is built from the bare stem and two suffixes.
intro.cn: 这里没有确定的前缀或词根，同族词由光裸词干加两个后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 湖；湖泊；（液体形成的）大片；（颜料）色淀
definition_en: a large area of water surrounded by land, also a broad expanse of liquid, and a technical word for a colour pigment
core_image: 山谷底下一整片静水，把对岸的山影完整地收在里面
scene: 雨后的山谷里，水面平得像一面镜子。By the lake, a fisherman was mending his net in the early light.
sceneCN: 这里 lake 指「湖、湖泊」（第 1 个义项）；句意为清晨湖边有个渔夫在补网。图中可辨识物件：静水面、对岸山影、渔网。

derivatives.zh: 由 lake 加表示「人」的 -er 构成，指湖畔居民或湖区来的人
由 lake 与 land 复合，指湖泊众多的地区
由 lake 与 front 复合，指临湖的前沿地带、湖滨

senses.title: A large area of water surrounded by land
senses.definition: a large area of water with land all around it, usually fresh water and not the sea
senses.definitionCN: 四周被陆地环绕的大片水域，通常为淡水而非海洋
senses.example: By the lake, a fisherman was mending his net in the early light.
senses.exampleCN: 清晨湖边有个渔夫在补网。
senses.why: Latin lacus named a basin or a body of standing water, and that single image of water held inside a hollow still shapes the everyday sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 lacus 指盆地或一片静水，这种「水被洼地兜住」的画面至今仍是日常义项的骨架。

senses.title: A broad expanse of liquid
senses.definition: a wide sheet of liquid spread over a surface, used mainly in descriptive writing
senses.definitionCN: 铺展在表面上的大片液体，多用于描写性文字
senses.example: A lake of spilled oil spread across the garage floor.
senses.exampleCN: 洒出的油在车库地面上摊成一大片。
senses.why: Anything that pools and spreads without a bank to hold it repeats the look of a lake, so the word stretches from real water to any wide sheet of liquid.
senses.whyCN: 凡是聚成一片、四下铺开又没有岸拦着的东西，都重复了湖的样子，于是词义从真正的水面延伸到任意大片液体。

senses.title: A solid colour pigment
senses.definition: a pigment made by fixing a dye onto a metallic base, used in paints and inks
senses.definitionCN: 把染料固定在金属基体上制成的颜料，用于油漆和油墨
senses.example: The painter mixed a red lake with linseed oil.
senses.exampleCN: 画家把一种红色色淀与亚麻油调在一起。
senses.why: This sense arrived by a separate route through French laque from Arabic lakk, so it is a homonym of the water word rather than a child of it.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项经法语 laque 从阿拉伯语 lakk 另走一条路进入英语，因此它只是水义同形的同音词，并非由水义生长而来。

intro.en: Lake comes from Latin lacus by way of Old French, while the pigment sense is a separate borrowing that happens to share the same spelling.
intro.cn: lake 经古法语来自拉丁语 lacus；颜料义则是另一次借入，只是碰巧拼写相同。

items.en: Lacus meant a lake, a basin or a reservoir, and it is the source of the word family across the Romance languages.
items.cn: lacus 指湖、盆地或蓄水池，是罗曼语族这一词族的来源。

items.en: Old French kept the word as lac, meaning lake, and Norman rule carried it across the Channel.
items.cn: 古法语保留为 lac，意为湖，诺曼统治把它带过海峡。

items.en: Middle English lake named a body of standing water, and the spelling settled in the form we use today.
items.cn: 中古英语 lake 指一片静水，拼写定型为今天使用的形式。

items.en: Dyers and painters took a second word, French laque from Arabic lakk, for a solid pigment, and English spelled it like the water word.
items.cn: 十六七世纪，染匠和画家为固体颜料引入另一个词——源自阿拉伯语 lakk 的法语 laque，英语把它拼得与「湖」一样。

items.en: Modern English uses lake chiefly for a large inland sheet of water, while the pigment sense survives as a technical term in art and dyeing.
items.cn: 现代英语的 lake 主要指大片内陆水域，颜料义则作为艺术与染色领域的术语留存。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the Latin water root or on the same spelling; the near-meaning group collects other bodies of water.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁「水」词根或同一拼写上的词；近义组收其他水域名称。

entries.definition: Relating to lakes, used in scientific writing.
entries.definitionCN: 与湖泊有关的，多用于科学写作。

entries.definition: Shallow water separated from the sea by sand or reef.
entries.definitionCN: 被沙洲或礁石与海隔开的浅水区。

entries.definition: A resinous substance secreted by an insect, unrelated to the water word.
entries.definitionCN: 一种昆虫分泌的树脂状物质，与「湖」这个词无关。

entries.definition: A small area of still water, usually smaller than a lake.
entries.definitionCN: 小片静水，通常比湖小。

entries.definition: A small area of water, often one that has collected naturally.
entries.definitionCN: 一小片水，常指自然聚成的水洼。

entries.definition: A large artificial lake used to store water for a city.
entries.definitionCN: 为城市储水而建的大型人工湖。

entries.definition: A lake or a pond, used mainly in names and older writing.
entries.definitionCN: 湖或池塘，多用于地名和较早的文学语言。

normalIntro.en: The water word rests on a Latin root for basin, and the pigment sense joined it later by a completely different road.
normalIntro.cn: 表示水的这个词建立在拉丁语「盆地」词根上，颜料义则是后来从完全不同的路径加进来的。

normal.en: Lacus in Latin is a basin of water, so a lake is water held inside a hollow of land.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 lacus 是一盆水，所以湖就是被陆地凹处兜住的水。

normal.en: Lacustrine is the scientific adjective from the same root, used for plants and sediments of lakes.
normal.cn: lacustrine 是同根词根构成的科学形容词，用于湖泊的植物与沉积物。

normal.en: A lagoon is a shallow sheet of water cut off from the sea, a cousin of the same Latin family.
normal.cn: lagoon 是被隔开的浅水，是同一拉丁词族的表亲。

normal.en: The pigment lake is spelled alike but comes through Arabic lakk, so the two words only look related.
normal.cn: 颜料义的 lake 拼写相同，却经阿拉伯语 lakk 而来，两个词只是看起来相关。

normal.en: Because a lake has no current, the word also describes anything that spreads and lies still, such as spilled oil.
normal.cn: 湖没有水流，所以这个词也能形容任何铺开静止的东西，比如洒出的油。

abstract.en: A hollow in the ground plus water equals a lake: the shape of the land decides that the water must stay.
abstract.cn: 地上的凹处加上水就是湖：是地形的形状决定了水必须留下。

abstract.en: The same spelling can hide two histories, and only the dictionary can tell which water is which.
abstract.cn: 同一个拼写可以藏着两段历史，只有词典能说清哪一片水来自哪里。

abstract.en: Still water reflects the whole hill, which is why lakes are the landscape's memory.
abstract.cn: 静水能映出整座山，所以湖是风景的记忆。

examples.en: By the lake, a fisherman was mending his net in the early light.
examples.cn: 清晨湖边有个渔夫在补网。

examples.en: The lake froze solid by the middle of January.
examples.cn: 一月中旬湖面就冻得结结实实。

examples.en: A lake of spilled oil spread across the garage floor.
examples.cn: 洒出的油在车库地面上摊成一大片。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「累客」——走累了的旅客在湖边歇脚；谐音记住 lake 是湖。

root: 拉丁语 lacus（湖、盆地、蓄水池）经古法语 lac 进入英语；颜料义的 lake 另源自阿拉伯语 lakk，属同形异源词。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is water held in a basin of land; the word then widens to any broad sheet of liquid and also names a dye-based pigment through a separate borrowing.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是被陆地兜住的水；词义随后扩展到任何大片液体，又经另一次借入指染料制成的色淀。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a still sheet of water lying inside a ring of hills.
core.cn: 核心意象：一圈山丘之间平躺着的一大片静水。

branches.en: a fisherman mending nets at first light
branches.cn: 天刚亮时补网的渔夫

branches.en: a hill reflected whole in still water
branches.cn: 整座山完整地映在静水里

branches.en: oil spreading flat across a garage floor
branches.cn: 油在车库地面上摊平

branches.en: a lake of blood in a battle description
branches.cn: 战事描写里的一片血泊

branches.en: a painter mixing a red pigment with oil
branches.cn: 画家把红色色淀与油调在一起

intro.en: The water word is a Latin noun that passed through French; the pigment word is a separate borrowing, and both are shown here because they share a spelling.
intro.cn: 水义是经法语而来的拉丁名词；颜料义是另一次借入，两者拼写相同，所以一并列出。

latinIntro.en: Lacus is the recorded Latin source of the water sense; lacuna is a probable relative meaning a pit or pool, though the link is usually described as uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: lacus 是有记录的水义拉丁来源；lacuna 意为坑或水洼，一般认为与之相关，但这一联系常被标注为不确定。

items.meaning: shallow water cut off from the sea

definition_zh: 羔羊；小羊；羔羊肉；温顺的人
definition_en: a young sheep; its meat as food; a gentle or innocent person; a religious image of sacrifice
core_image: 刚出生不久的小羊贴在母羊身边，毛还湿着
scene: 清晨的羊圈里，一只小羊跟在母羊身后，叫声又轻又软。The lamb pressed close to its mother as the farmer opened the gate.
sceneCN: 这里是「羔羊、小羊」（第 1 个义项：年幼的羊）；句意是农夫打开栅栏时，小羊紧紧贴着母羊。图中可辨识物件：羊圈木门、母羊、草垛。

pos.zh: 羔羊；小羊；羔羊肉；温顺的人

derivatives.zh: 由 lamb 加 -ing 构成，义为「产羔；产羔期」
由 lamb 与 skin 复合而成，义为「羔羊皮」
由 lamb 与 like 复合而成，义为「温顺如羔羊的」

senses.title: A young sheep
senses.definition: a young sheep, especially one that is less than a year old
senses.definitionCN: 年幼的羊，尤指不满一岁的小羊
senses.example: The lamb stayed close to its mother in the cold wind.
senses.exampleCN: 冷风里，小羊紧紧贴着母羊。
senses.why: The word has named the young sheep since Old English, and that animal is still the sense people picture first.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从古英语起就指年幼的羊，而这只动物仍是人们最先想到的义项。

senses.title: The meat of a young sheep
senses.definition: the meat of a young sheep, used as food
senses.definitionCN: 幼羊的肉，供人食用
senses.example: We had roast lamb with potatoes on Sunday.
senses.exampleCN: 星期天我们吃了烤羔羊肉配土豆。
senses.why: Once an animal is farmed for food, its name easily moves from the living creature to the meat on the plate.
senses.whyCN: 一种动物被饲养供食之后，它的名字很容易从活着的动物转到盘子里的肉。

senses.title: A gentle or innocent person
senses.definition: a meek, innocent or easily led person, often with a touch of irony
senses.definitionCN: 温顺、天真或容易被人牵着走的人，常带一点讽刺
senses.example: He followed her advice like a lamb.
senses.exampleCN: 他像小羊一样乖乖听了她的建议。
senses.why: A lamb is proverbially meek, so the animal's docility is transferred to a person who offers no resistance.
senses.whyCN: 小羊向来被视为温顺，于是这种驯顺被转用到毫不反抗的人身上。

senses.title: A religious image of sacrifice
senses.definition: a lamb used as a religious image of innocence or sacrifice, especially in Christian tradition
senses.definitionCN: 宗教中象征纯洁或祭献的羔羊，尤见于基督教传统
senses.example: The choir sang about the Lamb of God.
senses.exampleCN: 唱诗班唱起了关于上帝羔羊的歌。
senses.why: In biblical language a lamb offered in sacrifice became a picture of innocence given up for others, which fixed this symbolic sense in English.
senses.whyCN: 在圣经语言里，献祭的羔羊成了为他人舍去纯洁的象征，这个象征义因此在英语中固定下来。

intro.en: Lamb is a Germanic word for the young sheep; it never had a Latin twin, and English added meat, character and religious meanings to it.
intro.cn: lamb 是日耳曼语中指小羊的词，从未有拉丁语同形词，英语又给它添上肉食、性格与宗教含义。

items.en: A very old root is often reconstructed behind the word, but its exact form is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个词背后常被重构出一个非常古老的词根，但确切形式并不确定。

items.en: The Germanic form is reconstructed as lambaz, naming a young sheep.
items.cn: 日耳曼语形式通常重构为 lambaz，指年幼的羊。

items.en: Old English lamb already meant a young sheep and appears in early farming and religious texts.
items.cn: 古英语 lamb 已指小羊，见于早期农事与宗教文本。

items.en: Middle English kept lamb unchanged, and the plural lambs settled into the regular English pattern.
items.cn: 中古英语沿用 lamb 的拼写，复数 lambs 也固定为规则形式。

items.en: Modern English uses lamb for the animal, its meat, a meek person and a religious image.
items.cn: 现代英语用 lamb 指小羊、羔羊肉、温顺的人和宗教意象。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built from lamb and one accidental spelling neighbour; the near-meaning group gathers other sheep words.
note.cn: 形近组收由 lamb 构成的词和一个只是拼写相邻的词；近义组收其他与羊有关的词。

entries.definition: The skin of a lamb, used for leather or parchment.
entries.definitionCN: 羔羊的皮，可做皮革或羊皮纸。

entries.definition: The season or process of a ewe giving birth to lambs.
entries.definitionCN: 母羊产羔的季节或过程。

entries.definition: Gentle and docile in the way of a lamb.
entries.definitionCN: 像小羊一样温顺驯良的。

entries.definition: Of light or flame: soft and lightly dancing; only the spelling is close, with a different Latin history.
entries.definitionCN: 指光或火焰柔和而轻轻跳动；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The adult animal kept for wool and meat.
entries.definitionCN: 为取毛和肉而饲养的成年羊。

entries.definition: A female sheep, especially one old enough to breed.
entries.definitionCN: 母羊，尤指已到繁殖年龄的母羊。

entries.definition: A male sheep, often with large curled horns.
entries.definitionCN: 公羊，常长有大而卷曲的角。

normalIntro.en: The word stays close to the farm; its family adds the season of birth, the skin and the quality of meekness.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词始终贴近农事；它的词族添上产羔季节、羊皮和温顺的性质。

normal.en: Old English lamb is one of the oldest farming words in English, so the animal sense comes before every metaphor.
normal.cn: 古英语 lamb 是英语中最古老的农事词之一，所以动物义先于所有比喻义。

normal.en: The plural is lambs, not lambes, because the word ends in a plain voiced sound rather than a hissing one.
normal.cn: 复数是 lambs 而不是 lambes，因为词尾是普通的浊音，而不是嘶嘶的咝音。

normal.en: Lambing names the season when ewes give birth, which is why the suffix -ing here means a period of activity.
normal.cn: lambing 指母羊生产的季节，所以这里的后缀 -ing 表示一段活动时期。

normal.en: Lambskin is simply lamb plus skin, and it names the hide rather than the living animal.
normal.cn: lambskin 就是 lamb 加 skin，指的是皮张而不是活着的动物。

normal.en: Like a lamb is the phrase that carries the meekness sense, and it often sounds gently ironic.
normal.cn: like a lamb 是承载温顺义的短语，听起来常带一点温和的讽刺。

abstract.en: An animal born helpless becomes a picture of innocence, and from there a picture of sacrifice.
abstract.cn: 一种生来无助的动物先成为纯洁的图画，再由此成为牺牲的图画。

abstract.en: The same word can name a living creature, a meal and a person's character, because farming binds all three together.
abstract.cn: 同一个词能指活物、餐食和人的性格，因为农事把这三者绑在一起。

abstract.en: Lamb shows how a plain farm word can carry a whole moral vocabulary without ever leaving the pen.
abstract.cn: lamb 说明一个朴素的农事词可以承载整套道德语汇，却始终没有离开羊圈。

examples.en: The lamb stayed close to its mother in the cold wind.
examples.cn: 冷风里，小羊紧紧贴着母羊。

examples.en: We had roast lamb with potatoes on Sunday.
examples.cn: 星期天我们吃了烤羔羊肉配土豆。

examples.en: He followed her advice like a lamb.
examples.cn: 他像小羊一样乖乖听了她的建议。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拉姆」——球场上有个叫拉姆的球员，像小羊一样温顺；lamb 是羔羊。

root: 古英语 lamb，源自日耳曼语 lambaz，与荷兰语 lam、德语 Lamm 同族；没有可靠的拉丁语同源词。

sensesIntro.en: The young sheep is the core; the senses divide into its meat, a meek person, and the religious lamb of sacrifice.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是年幼的羊；义项由此分出它的肉、温顺的人，以及宗教中献祭的羔羊。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a newborn lamb standing close against its mother's flank.
core.cn: 核心意象：刚出生的小羊紧紧靠在本羊的腹侧。

branches.en: a newborn animal wobbling on its first legs
branches.cn: 刚出生的小羊在初生的腿上摇晃

branches.en: a farm where some animals are kept and some are sold
branches.cn: 既留养一些羊又卖掉一些羊的农场

branches.en: a Sunday table with roast meat and potatoes
branches.cn: 星期天摆着烤肉和土豆的餐桌

branches.en: a person who never says no
branches.cn: 一个从不说「不」的人

branches.en: an altar where innocence is offered up
branches.cn: 献上纯洁的祭坛

intro.en: A Germanic noun gains one suffix for the birth season and two compounds for skin and for character.
intro.cn: 这个日耳曼语名词靠一个后缀表示产羔季节，靠两个复合词表示皮张与性格。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: the season of giving birth to lambs

items.meaningCN: 名词后缀：动作或活动时期

items.meaning: a cut of meat from a lamb
a dish of lamb cooked slowly

definition_zh: 灯；灯具；灯泡；明灯
definition_en: a device that produces light, the light source inside it, or a light used as a symbol of guidance
core_image: 夜里书桌上一盏小灯，把纸页照出一圈柔和的光
scene: 屋里突然停电，只有桌角那盏油灯还亮着。She turned up the lamp and went on reading.
sceneCN: 这里是「灯」（第 1 个义项：照明的器具）；句意为她把灯芯调亮，继续读书。可辨识画面：停电的房间、桌角的油灯、翻开的书页。

derivatives.zh: 由 lamp 与 light 复合，义为「灯光」
由 lamp 与 shade 复合，义为「灯罩」
由 lamp 加 -lit（被照亮的）构成，义为「灯光照亮的」

senses.title: A device that gives light
senses.definition: an object, often with a base and a bulb, that produces light
senses.definitionCN: 通常带底座与灯泡、用来发光的器具
senses.example: He switched on the lamp beside the bed.
senses.exampleCN: 他打开了床边的灯。
senses.why: Greek lampas named a torch, something carried to make light, and that portable source is still the core of the word.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 lampas 指火把，即随身携带照明的物件，这个词的核心至今仍是可移动的光源。

senses.title: The light source inside a lamp
senses.definition: the bulb or tube inside a lamp that actually glows
senses.definitionCN: 灯内部真正发光的灯泡或灯管
senses.example: One lamp in the ceiling fixture had burned out.
senses.exampleCN: 天花板灯具里有一只灯泡烧坏了。
senses.why: Because people name the whole device and its glowing part together, the word for the device slid onto the part that shines.
senses.whyCN: 因为人们把整套器具与发光的部件一起提及，器具的名字就滑到了发光的零件上。

senses.title: A guiding light, used figuratively
senses.definition: a person or idea that gives guidance, like a light in darkness
senses.definitionCN: 在黑暗中给人指引的人或理念
senses.example: Her letters were a lamp through those dark months.
senses.exampleCN: 在那些灰暗的月份里，她的来信是一盏明灯。
senses.why: A lamp is what you follow when you cannot see the road, so the word naturally stands for anything that shows the way.
senses.whyCN: 看不清路的时候，人会跟着灯走，所以这个词自然用来指任何指明方向的东西。

senses.title: A lamp used for treatment
senses.definition: a device emitting heat or ultraviolet light for medical or technical use
senses.definitionCN: 用于医疗或技术、发出热或紫外光的装置
senses.example: The clinic uses a lamp to warm the injured muscle.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所使用理疗灯为受伤的肌肉加温。
senses.why: Once a lamp is a controlled source of rays rather than a household object, the same word serves clinics and workshops.
senses.whyCN: 当灯变成可控制的射线来源而不再是家用物件，同一个词就服务于诊所与车间。

intro.en: Lamp travels from a Greek word for torch, through Latin and French, to the small light on a modern desk.
intro.cn: lamp 从希腊语表示火把的词出发，经拉丁语与法语，走到现代书桌上的那盏小灯。

items.en: Lampas meant a torch or a light, and it was built on a verb meaning to shine.
items.cn: lampas 意为火把、光，由表示发光的动词构成。

items.en: Lampein meant to shine or to give light, the verb behind the noun.
items.cn: lampein 意为发光、照亮，是名词背后的动词。

items.en: Latin borrowed lampas for a torch or lamp and kept the sense of shining.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 lampas，指火把或灯，保留了发光的意味。

items.en: Old French lampe named the oil lamp, and English took the word in the Middle Ages.
items.cn: 古法语 lampe 指烧油的灯，中世纪时进入英语。

items.en: Modern English uses lamp for lamps of every kind and for the glow inside them.
items.cn: 现代英语用 lamp 指各种灯，也指灯里发出的光。

note.en: The look-alike group collects short words with a similar shape; the near-meaning group collects other words for lights and light sources.
note.cn: 形近组收形状相近的短词；近义组收表示灯具与光源的其他用词。

entries.definition: A young sheep; the spelling is close but the history is unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 小羊；拼写相近，词源无关。

entries.definition: To walk unevenly because of a hurt leg.
entries.definitionCN: 因腿受伤而走路不稳。

entries.definition: A small solid mass of something.
entries.definitionCN: 一小块固体的东西。

entries.definition: A piece of writing that makes fun of someone.
entries.definitionCN: 讥讽某人的文字作品。

entries.definition: The general word for brightness that lets you see.
entries.definitionCN: 表示光亮、让人看得见的一般用词。

entries.definition: A lamp inside a protective case, often carried by hand.
entries.definitionCN: 装在保护外壳里、常被手提着的灯。

entries.definition: A burning stick used for light, or a hand-held electric light.
entries.definitionCN: 用作照明的燃烧木棒，或手电筒。

entries.definition: The glass part of a lamp that glows.
entries.definitionCN: 灯里发光的玻璃部件。

normalIntro.en: A Greek torch and a Greek verb of shining hold the word together, and modern compounds keep the household sense alive.
normalIntro.cn: 一个希腊语的火把与一个希腊语的发光动词支撑着这个词，现代复合词则让家用义延续。

normal.en: Greek lampas was a torch, so lamp begins as something you carry in order to see.
normal.cn: 希腊语 lampas 是火把，所以 lamp 起于一件为了看清而随身携带的物件。

normal.en: The verb lampein meant to shine, and the noun lampas was built on that shining.
normal.cn: 动词 lampein 意为发光，名词 lampas 就建立在这层「发光」上。

normal.en: Table lamp and street lamp follow one pattern: place or use first, lamp second.
normal.cn: table lamp 与 street lamp 遵循同一构造：先写地点或用途，再写 lamp。

normal.en: Lampshade is lamp plus shade, the thing that shades the light.
normal.cn: lampshade 是 lamp 加 shade，即给光加上遮挡的罩子。

normal.en: Lamplit is lamp plus lit: a street that is lit by lamps.
normal.cn: lamplit 是 lamp 加 lit，指被灯照亮的街道。

abstract.en: A lamp is borrowed light: one small flame is made to stand in for the sun.
abstract.cn: 灯是借来的光：它让一小簇火苗代替太阳。

abstract.en: Because people follow a lamp when they cannot see, the word easily becomes a metaphor for guidance.
abstract.cn: 因为看不清时我们会跟着灯走，这个词很容易变成指引的比喻。

abstract.en: The word travels from torch to bulb, showing how a name stays while the technology under it changes.
abstract.cn: 这个词从火把走到灯泡，说明名字可以不变，而底下的技术在变。

examples.en: He switched on the lamp beside the bed.
examples.cn: 他打开了床边的灯。

examples.en: The street lamps come on at dusk.
examples.cn: 黄昏时路灯亮起。

examples.en: Her letters were a lamp through those dark months.
examples.cn: 在那些灰暗的月份里，她的来信是一盏明灯。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拦」——夜里走路先拦下一盏灯看清脚下；记住 lamp 是灯。

root: 希腊语 lampas（火把、光），来自动词 lampein（发光），经拉丁语 lampas 与古法语 lampe 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a portable light; the senses then split into the whole device, the glowing part, a figurative guide, and lamps built for treatment.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一件可移动的光源；义项由此分为整件器具、发光的部件、比喻性的指引，以及用于治疗的灯。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small flame under a glass shade on a dark table.
core.cn: 核心意象：暗桌上一只玻璃罩下的小火苗。

branches.en: a lamp burning on a bedside table
branches.cn: 床头柜上亮着的灯

branches.en: a burnt-out bulb in a ceiling fixture
branches.cn: 天花板灯具里烧坏的灯泡

branches.en: a letter read by someone in a dark year
branches.cn: 在灰暗岁月里被读到的一封信

branches.en: a red lamp warming a sore shoulder
branches.cn: 照在酸痛肩膀上的理疗红灯

branches.en: a hand reaching for the switch in the dark
branches.cn: 黑暗中伸手去摸开关的手

intro.en: A Greek noun of torch, a Greek verb of shining, and the English endings that build compounds hold this word together.
intro.cn: 一个表示火把的希腊名词、一个表示发光的希腊动词，以及造出复合词的英语词尾，共同支撑着这个词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: a cover that shades a lamp
a post holding a street lamp

definition_zh: 陆地；土地；国土；登陆；着陆
definition_en: the solid surface of the earth, ground or a country, or to come down onto the ground
core_image: 船头前方浮出一条灰绿色的海岸线，脚下的甲板终于能换成泥土
scene: 飞机穿过云层，跑道在下方一点点变大。The plane landed safely on the runway.
sceneCN: 这里是「着陆、降落」（第 4 个义项：动词，指飞行器触地停下）；句意为飞机安全地降落在跑道上。图中可辨识物件：云层、跑道、正在下降的飞机。

derivatives.zh: 由 land 加 -ing 构成，义为「着陆；登陆；楼梯平台」
由 land 与 -scape（景色）复合，义为「风景；景观」
由 land 与 lord 复合，义为「地主；房东」
由 main 与 land 复合，义为「大陆；本土」

senses.title: The solid surface of the earth
senses.definition: the part of the earth's surface that is not covered by water
senses.definitionCN: 地球表面没有被水覆盖的部分
senses.example: After weeks at sea, the sailors finally saw land.
senses.exampleCN: 在海上漂了几周之后，水手们终于看见了陆地。
senses.why: Land begins as the dry ground that a boat can reach, a boundary between water and solid earth.
senses.whyCN: land 最初指船只能抵达的干燥地面，是水与坚实大地之间的分界。

senses.title: Ground used for a purpose
senses.definition: ground owned or used by someone, especially for farming or building
senses.definitionCN: 某人拥有或使用的土地，尤指用于耕种或建造
senses.example: The family has farmed this land for three generations.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人在这块土地上耕种了三代。
senses.why: Once land means solid ground, it can be divided, owned and worked, so the word comes to mean a piece of ground with a use.
senses.whyCN: 既然 land 指坚实的地面，就可以被划分、拥有和耕作，于是它转而指一块有用途的地。

senses.title: A country or nation
senses.definition: a country, especially one thought of as the home of a people
senses.definitionCN: 国家，尤指被视为一个民族家园的国土
senses.example: She returned to her native land after many years abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 在国外多年之后，她回到了故土。
senses.why: A people's ground is their country, so land shifts from soil to the political and emotional idea of a homeland.
senses.whyCN: 一个民族脚下的土地就是他们的国家，于是 land 从泥土转到「故土」这一政治与情感概念。

senses.title: To come down to the ground
senses.definition: to come to the ground from the air or from water, especially after a flight
senses.definitionCN: 从空中或水上来到地面，尤指飞行之后
senses.example: The plane landed safely on the runway.
senses.exampleCN: 飞机安全地降落在跑道上。
senses.why: The noun names the ground; the verb reverses the direction and means reaching that ground, as a plane or a boat does.
senses.whyCN: 名词指地面；动词把方向反过来，表示抵达地面，飞机或船就是这样。

senses.title: To succeed in getting something
senses.definition: to succeed in obtaining a job, a contract or an opportunity
senses.definitionCN: 成功得到工作、合同或机会
senses.example: He landed a good job at a design studio.
senses.exampleCN: 他在一家设计工作室找到了一份好工作。
senses.why: To land a job is to bring something down and secure it, like a plane touching the ground after a search.
senses.whyCN: land a job 就像飞机经过搜寻后触地一样，把某样东西稳稳弄到手。

intro.en: Land is an Old English word shared across the Germanic languages, with a deep but partly reconstructed root.
intro.cn: land 是古英语词，在日耳曼语族中广泛共享，其更深词根有一部分属于重构形式。

items.en: Land meant earth, territory or a country, and it already carried both the physical and the political sense.
items.cn: land 意为土地、领土或国家，已经同时带有自然与政治两层意思。

items.en: The reconstructed Germanic form *landa is shared by German Land and Dutch land.
items.cn: 重构的日耳曼语形式 *landa 为德语 Land 与荷兰语 land 所共享。

items.en: The deeper root is reconstructed as *lendh-, meaning land or heath, but the reconstruction is not certain.
items.cn: 更深的词根被重构为 *lendh-，意为土地或荒地，但这一重构并不确定。

items.en: Middle English keeps land for ground and country and begins to use it as a verb for coming ashore.
items.cn: 中古英语保留 land 表示土地与国家，并开始把它用作「上岸」的动词。

items.en: Modern English adds landing, landscape and landlord, and extends the verb to planes and jobs.
items.cn: 现代英语添上 landing、landscape、landlord，并把动词扩展到飞机与工作。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on land; the near-meaning group gathers words for ground, country and coming down.
note.cn: 形近组收以 land 构成的词；近义组收表示土地、国家与降落的词。

entries.definition: The act of coming down to the ground, or a flat area at the top of stairs.
entries.definitionCN: 着陆；楼梯平台。

entries.definition: The visible features of an area of land.
entries.definitionCN: 风景；景观。

entries.definition: A person who owns property and rents it to others.
entries.definitionCN: 地主；房东。

entries.definition: The main mass of land, as opposed to islands.
entries.definitionCN: 大陆；本土。

entries.definition: The solid surface beneath the feet.
entries.definitionCN: 地面。

entries.definition: The upper layer of earth in which plants grow.
entries.definitionCN: 土壤。

entries.definition: A nation with its own government and territory.
entries.definitionCN: 国家。

entries.definition: The land along the edge of a sea or lake.
entries.definitionCN: 岸；海滨。

normalIntro.en: One short Germanic word covers ground, country and the act of touching down, and its compounds make the connections visible.
normalIntro.cn: 一个简短的日耳曼词同时覆盖土地、国家与触地，复合词把这些联系摆了出来。

normal.en: Land is both noun and verb: the land, to land.
normal.cn: land 名动同形：the land 与 to land。

normal.en: Landscape joins land to -scape, a suffix for a view or scene.
normal.cn: landscape 把 land 与表示景色的 -scape 组合。

normal.en: Landlord joins land to lord: the owner of the ground.
normal.cn: landlord 把 land 与 lord 组合，指土地的主人。

normal.en: Landing adds -ing and names both the act and the place where you step down.
normal.cn: landing 加 -ing，既指着陆动作，也指落脚的平台。

normal.en: To land a job keeps the idea of a plane touching down after a search.
normal.cn: land a job 保留飞机经过搜寻后触地的意象。

abstract.en: The same word serves soil, nation and arrival because all three are places where movement stops.
abstract.cn: 同一个词同时服务泥土、国家与抵达，因为三者都是运动停下来的地方。

abstract.en: Owning land turns a physical surface into a legal and emotional object.
abstract.cn: 拥有土地把一个物理表面变成为法律与情感的对象。

abstract.en: A landing is a boundary event: above and below meet for a moment.
abstract.cn: landing 是一个边界事件：上与下短暂地相接。

examples.en: After weeks at sea, the sailors finally saw land.
examples.cn: 在海上漂了几周之后，水手们终于看见了陆地。

examples.en: The plane landed safely on the runway.
examples.cn: 飞机安全地降落在跑道上。

examples.en: He landed a good job at a design studio.
examples.cn: 他在一家设计工作室找到了一份好工作。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「兰德」——音译成「兰德」，脚下踩的陆地就叫 land。

root: 古英语 land（土地、国土），与德语 Land、荷兰语 land 同源；更深词根 *lendh- 为重构形式，来源不完全确定。

sensesIntro.en: The core is solid ground; the senses move from ground to owned soil, to a people's country, then to the act of reaching ground and getting hold of something.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是坚实的地面；义项由地面转到可拥有的土地，再到民族的国土，最后到触地与「弄到手」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grey-green coastline appearing ahead of a boat, and a deck finally replaced by soil.
core.cn: 核心意象：船头前方浮出灰绿色的海岸线，甲板终于换成泥土。

branches.en: a strip of shore seen from the deck
branches.cn: 从甲板上望见的一条岸

branches.en: a field divided by low stone walls
branches.cn: 矮石墙分隔的田地

branches.en: a map with a name printed across it
branches.cn: 印着国名的地图

branches.en: wheels meeting the runway
branches.cn: 机轮触到跑道

branches.en: a hand closing on a contract
branches.cn: 手握紧一份合同

intro.en: The word is a Germanic stem that forms a large family by compounding rather than by adding long affixes.
intro.cn: 这个词是日耳曼词干，靠复合而不是长词缀形成一大族词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: act of coming down; stair platform

definition_zh: 房东；地主；（旧）旅店老板；客栈掌柜
definition_en: the person who owns a house or room and lets it to tenants, also a dated word for an innkeeper or the owner of land
core_image: 一个人站在自家楼门口，手里捏着一串钥匙和一沓房租收据
scene: 冬天的清晨，楼道里的暖气还没热起来。The landlord knocked on the door to collect the rent.
sceneCN: 这里 landlord 指「房东」（第 1 个义项）；句意为房东敲门来收房租。图中可辨识物件：楼门、钥匙串、房租收据。

derivatives.zh: 由 land 与 lady 复合，指女房东、女店主
由 landlord 加 -ism 构成，指地主收租的制度
由 landlord 加 -ing 构成，指出租房屋收租的行当

senses.title: The owner of property that is rented out
senses.definition: the person who owns a house, flat or room and lets it to someone who pays rent
senses.definitionCN: 拥有房屋、公寓或房间并出租给交租金者的人
senses.example: The landlord knocked on the door to collect the rent.
senses.exampleCN: 房东敲门来收房租。
senses.why: Once houses were let for money, the man who held the land also held the keys, so the compound shifted from owning ground to receiving rent.
senses.whyCN: 当房屋开始出租换钱，握有土地的人也握有钥匙，于是这个复合词从「拥有土地」转向「收取租金」。

senses.title: The keeper of an inn or a pub
senses.definition: a dated word for the man who runs an inn, a boarding house or a pub
senses.definitionCN: 较早的用法，指经营旅店、寄宿舍或酒馆的男子
senses.example: The landlord of the old inn kept a fire burning all winter.
senses.exampleCN: 那家老旅店的老板整个冬天都让炉火不灭。
senses.why: An innkeeper owned the building he worked in, so the word for a property owner naturally covered the man behind the bar.
senses.whyCN: 旅店老板拥有自己经营的房子，因此「房产所有者」这个词自然也能指吧台后面的那个人。

senses.title: The lord of a manor
senses.definition: a historical word for the man who held land from a superior and ruled the tenants on it
senses.definitionCN: 历史用法，指从上级领有土地并管束其佃户的男子
senses.example: The landlord of the manor also judged disputes among his tenants.
senses.exampleCN: 庄园领主还裁决佃户之间的纠纷。
senses.why: In the feudal order land carried power, so landlord named not just an owner but the man whose word settled what happened on his ground.
senses.whyCN: 在封建秩序里土地意味着权力，因此 landlord 不只指所有者，还指那个一句话就能决定自己地界上事务的人。

intro.en: Landlord is a Middle English compound of land and lord, and lord itself goes back to an Old English word for the keeper of the loaf.
intro.cn: landlord 是中古英语由 land 与 lord 构成的复合词，而 lord 又可追到古英语中「掌管面包者」一词。

items.en: Land meant ground, territory or a country, and it is one of the oldest Germanic words in English.
items.cn: land 指土地、领土或国家，是英语中最古老的日耳曼词之一。

items.en: Hlaford, the ancestor of lord, first meant the keeper of the loaf, the man who fed those who depended on him.
items.cn: lord 的前身 hlaford 最初意为「掌管面包的人」，即供养依附者的男子。

items.en: Middle English joined land and lord into one compound for the man who owned or held land.
items.cn: 中古英语把 land 与 lord 合为一个复合词，指拥有或持有土地的人。

items.en: As more houses were let for rent, landlord widened from the owner of land to the owner of any rented property.
items.cn: 随着越来越多房屋出租，landlord 从土地所有者扩大到任何出租房产的所有者。

items.en: Modern English uses landlord for the person you pay rent to, and keeps the innkeeper sense in older or British pub use.
items.cn: 现代英语用 landlord 指收房租的人，旅店老板义则留在较早用法与英式酒馆说法里。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built on land or lord; the near-meaning group collects other words for people who own or manage property.
note.cn: 形近组收由 land 或 lord 构成的词；近义组收其他表示房产所有者或经营者的词。

entries.definition: A woman who owns property and lets it, or runs an inn.
entries.definitionCN: 女房东；女店主。

entries.definition: The system in which landlords take rent from tenants.
entries.definitionCN: 地主向佃户收租的制度。

entries.definition: A master or nobleman, the second half of this compound.
entries.definitionCN: 主人或贵族，是这个词的后一半。

entries.definition: A person who legally possesses something.
entries.definitionCN: 合法拥有某物的人。

entries.definition: The owner of a business or of property.
entries.definitionCN: 企业或房产的所有者。

entries.definition: A person who grants a lease of property.
entries.definitionCN: 出租房产并授予租约的人。

entries.definition: A person who runs an inn.
entries.definitionCN: 经营旅店的人。

normalIntro.en: The compound joins the oldest word for ground to the old word for a master, and its history moves from holding soil to collecting rent.
normalIntro.cn: 这个复合词把最古老的「土地」一词与古老的「主人」一词结合，其历史从持有土地走向收取租金。

normal.en: Land is the ground itself, one of the oldest Germanic words in English.
normal.cn: land 就是土地本身，是英语中最古老的日耳曼词之一。

normal.en: Lord began as hlaford, the keeper of the loaf, the man who fed his household.
normal.cn: lord 起初是 hlaford，即掌管面包、供养一家人的人。

normal.en: Landlord is literally the lord of the land, the man whose word ruled his ground.
normal.cn: landlord 字面就是「土地之主」，他的话在自己地界上说了算。

normal.en: When renting spread, the lord of the land became the man who collects rent, while keeping his keys.
normal.cn: 当租房普及，土地之主变成了收房租的人，钥匙也仍在他手里。

normal.en: Landlady adds the female counterpart, and landlordism names the system rather than a person.
normal.cn: landlady 提供女性对应形式，landlordism 指制度而非某个人。

abstract.en: A compound can carry a whole social order: land plus master equals power over the people who live on it.
abstract.cn: 一个复合词能装下整套社会秩序：土地加主人，等于对住在上面的人的支配权。

abstract.en: The word did not change owners; it changed what owning meant, from soil to rent.
abstract.cn: 这个词换的不是所有者，而是「拥有」的含义：从泥土变为租金。

abstract.en: Keys and rent receipts are the modern costume of an old feudal title.
abstract.cn: 钥匙与房租收据，是一个古老封建头衔的现代装扮。

examples.en: The landlord knocked on the door to collect the rent.
examples.cn: 房东敲门来收房租。

examples.en: She has not paid the landlord this month.
examples.cn: 她这个月还没把房租交给房东。

examples.en: The landlord of the old inn kept a fire burning all winter.
examples.cn: 那家老旅店的老板整个冬天都让炉火不灭。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「懒得劳动」——懒得劳动的地主靠收租过日子；谐音记住 landlord 是房东、地主。

root: 由古英语 land（土地）与 lord（前身 hlaford，掌管面包者）复合而成；指拥有土地或出租房产的人。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the man who holds land and lets others use it; from there it names the rent collector, the innkeeper and the feudal lord.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是持有土地并让别人使用的人；由此分出收房租者、旅店老板与封建领主。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a man at a doorway holding keys and a bundle of rent receipts.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在门口，手里拿着钥匙和一沓房租收据。

branches.en: a knock at the door on rent day
branches.cn: 收租日的一次敲门

branches.en: a tenant handing over an envelope of cash
branches.cn: 房客递上一个装现金的信封

branches.en: a manor court settling a dispute
branches.cn: 庄园法庭裁决一场纠纷

branches.en: a fire kept burning in an old inn
branches.cn: 老旅店里整夜不灭的炉火

branches.en: a pub keeper wiping the counter
branches.cn: 酒馆掌柜擦着柜台

intro.en: The word is a Germanic compound of two Old English nouns, and English suffixes later build abstract and feminine forms from it.
intro.cn: 这个词是两个古英语名词组成的日耳曼复合词，后来英语后缀又由它造出抽象名词与女性形式。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this compound; both of its parts are Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个复合词没有可靠的拉丁同族词，它的两个组成部分都属日耳曼语。

definition_zh: 风景；景观；地貌；（某一领域的）局面；（印刷、摄影）横向版式
definition_en: the visible features of an area of land; a picture representing such scenery; the overall pattern of a field of activity; (printing) a page format wider than it is tall
core_image: 从高处望下去，田野、河流与道路拼成一整幅画
scene: 地理课上，老师把投影切成一幅航拍图。The valley landscape was left behind by a retreating glacier.
sceneCN: 这里 landscape 是「地貌景观」（第 1 个义项：一片土地的可见形态）；句意：这条河谷景观是冰川退却后留下的。

pos.zh: 风景；景观；地貌（可数指一片景观，不可数指景观类型）
（某领域的）局面；横向版式（常带修饰语，如 political landscape）

derivatives.zh: 经景观设计的
景观布置；造景
景观设计师；园林工
海景；海景画
城市景观
月球表面景观

senses.title: Visible features of land
senses.definition: the shape, texture, and features of an area of land, including hills, rivers, fields, and vegetation
senses.definitionCN: 一片土地的形状、质地与特征，包括山丘、河流、田野与植被
senses.example: Glaciers shaped the landscape of this valley.
senses.exampleCN: 冰川塑造了这条河谷的地貌。
senses.why: Landscape is borrowed from Dutch landschap, land plus -schap, a suffix of state or condition cognate with English -ship. The word began as 'the condition of the land', which is why it can name both a region and how that region looks.
senses.whyCN: landscape 借自荷兰语 landschap，由 land 加 -schap 构成，后者是表示状态或状况的后缀，与英语 -ship 同源。这个词最初意为“土地的状况”，所以它既能命名一片区域，也能命名这片区域的样子。

senses.title: A landscape painting
senses.definition: a painting or photograph whose main subject is natural scenery
senses.definitionCN: 以自然景色为主要题材的绘画或摄影
senses.example: The museum bought a seventeenth-century Dutch landscape.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆买下一幅 17 世纪荷兰风景画。
senses.why: The word entered English in the sixteenth century as an art term: a picture of a land. Dutch painters made the genre famous, and the word travelled with the paintings.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在 16 世纪作为艺术术语进入英语：一幅关于土地的画。荷兰画家使这一画种闻名，词随画一起传来。

senses.title: Landscape in geography and ecology
senses.titleCN: 地理与生态学中的景观
senses.definition: an area considered as a system of interacting physical, biological, and human features
senses.definitionCN: 被视作物理、生物与人文特征交互系统的区域
senses.example: Landscape ecology studies how patches of habitat connect.
senses.exampleCN: 景观生态学研究栖息地斑块如何连接。
senses.why: Geography turned the word into a technical unit: a landscape is not just a view but a system with boundaries and flows. The visual sense survives inside the scientific one.
senses.whyCN: 地理学把这个词变成技术单位：景观不只是视野，而是有边界与流动的系统。视觉义在科学义内部存活下来。

senses.title: The pattern of a field of activity
senses.definition: the overall arrangement of forces, players, or conditions in a particular area of activity
senses.definitionCN: 某一活动领域中力量、参与者或条件的总体布局
senses.example: The merger changed the competitive landscape of the industry.
senses.exampleCN: 这次合并改变了该行业的竞争格局。
senses.why: Twentieth-century business and political writing borrowed the word for a field of play: competitors occupy positions the way hills occupy a view. The metaphor is spatial, and it treats the situation as something seen from above.
senses.whyCN: 20 世纪的商业与政治写作把这个词借来指一个竞技场：竞争者占据位置，就像山丘占据视野。这个比喻是空间性的，把局势当作从高处看到的东西。

senses.title: Landscape page format
senses.definition: a page or image orientation in which the width is greater than the height
senses.definitionCN: 宽度大于高度的页面或图像方向
senses.example: Print the map in landscape format so the whole route fits.
senses.exampleCN: 把地图打成横向版式，好让整条路线容纳进来。
