branches.en: THE HORTICULTURAL ACT: a stem is laid under soil so that it roots, turning the verb back into a physical laying-down.
branches.cn: 园艺动作：枝条被铺在土下以便生根，使动词回到物理上的“铺下”。

intro.en: Layer is an English compound of lay + -er. Its family is built with -ed, -ing, and the prefixes multi- and inter-.
intro.cn: layer 是 lay + -er 的英语复合词。它的词族用 -ed、-ing，以及前缀 multi-、inter- 构成。

latinIntro.en: Layer has no Latin root; it is native English. The Latin word for a geological layer is stratum, from sternere 'to spread out', which is a useful contrast rather than a source.
latinIntro.cn: layer 没有拉丁词根，是本族英语词。地质层的拉丁词是 stratum，来自 sternere“铺开”，这是有用的对照，而不是来源。

items.meaning: a sheet laid over a surface; one who lays
items.meaningCN: 层；放置者（-er 表施动者或事物）
items.example: A layer of ice formed on the pond.

items.meaning: several sheets or levels; the act of layering
items.meaningCN: 多层；分层（复数或第三人称单数）

items.example: The story has a layered structure.

items.meaning: the act of arranging in layers; plant propagation
items.example: Layering is a simple way to propagate plants.
items.exampleCN: 压条是一种简单的植物繁殖方法。
这种薄膜使用多层包装。

items.meaningCN: 夹层；中间层（inter- 表之间）
items.example: A thin interlayer separates the two sheets.
items.exampleCN: 一层薄薄的夹层把两片材料隔开。

items.meaning: a cake made of stacked layers
items.example: She baked a chocolate layer cake.
items.exampleCN: 她烤了一个巧克力千层蛋糕。

items.meaning: the atmospheric band rich in ozone
items.example: The ozone layer absorbs ultraviolet light.

items.meaningCN: 放置；铺下（layer 的基础动词）
items.example: She laid the cloth on the table.

latinEntries.meaning: a layer, bed, pavement (not the source of layer)
latinEntries.meaningCN: 层；地层（并非 layer 的来源，仅作对照）

latinEntries.meaning: bed, couch (same PIE root as lay)
latinEntries.meaningCN: 床；卧榻（与 lay 同出一个原始印欧语词根）

definition_zh: 布局；版面设计；布置；规划图
definition_en: the way in which parts of something are arranged; the arrangement of text and pictures on a page; a plan showing such an arrangement
core_image: 桌面上摊开的图纸，方块、线条和标注被摆成清楚的位置关系
scene: 设计师把桌上的草图推开一点，重新摆放照片和标题的位置。The designer changed the layout of the page to give the photos more room.
sceneCN: 这里是「版面布局」（第 1 个义项：各部分在页面上的安排）；句意是设计师调整了页面布局，给照片留出更多空间。图中可辨识物件：草图、照片、标题。

pos.zh: 布局；版面设计；布置；规划图

derivatives.zh: 由 lay 与 out 组成的短语动词，义为「布置；摊开；排版」
由 re- 与 layout 复合而成，义为「重新布局」
由 lay out 的过去分词形式构成，义为「布置好的；摊开的」

senses.title: The arrangement of text and pictures on a page
senses.definition: the way text, pictures and empty space are arranged on a page or screen
senses.definitionCN: 文字、图片与空白在页面或屏幕上的安排方式
senses.example: The designer changed the layout of the page to give the photos more room.
senses.exampleCN: 设计师调整了页面布局，给照片留出更多空间。
senses.why: Lay out first meant to spread things on a surface; printers then used it for placing type and images, and the noun kept that page sense.
senses.whyCN: lay out 最初指把东西摊在平面上；印刷者随后用它指摆放字与图，名词便保留了这层页面义。

senses.title: The way parts of a place are arranged
senses.definition: the arrangement of furniture, rooms or objects within a space
senses.definitionCN: 家具、房间或物件在某一空间内的安排
senses.example: The new layout of the kitchen puts the sink under the window.
senses.exampleCN: 厨房的新布局把水槽放到了窗下。
senses.why: A room is laid out much like a page: things are placed in relation to one another, and the same noun serves both.
senses.whyCN: 房间的布置很像页面的排版：物件按彼此关系摆放，同一个名词便兼指两者。

senses.title: A plan or diagram of an arrangement
senses.definition: a drawing or plan that shows how something is or will be arranged
senses.definitionCN: 表明某物现状或未来安排方式的图样或规划
senses.example: The engineer handed us a layout of the factory floor.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师递给我们一张车间平面布置图。
senses.why: Once an arrangement is fixed, it can be drawn; the drawing takes the same name because it records the very placement the word describes.
senses.whyCN: 安排一旦确定就能画成图；图纸沿用同一个名字，因为它记录的正是这个词所描述的摆放方式。

intro.en: Layout is a nineteenth-century English compound: the verb lay out, meaning to spread or arrange, became a noun for the arrangement itself.
intro.cn: layout 是十九世纪的英语复合词：短语动词 lay out（摊开、布置）变成了指安排本身的名词。

items.en: Lay comes from the Old English verb lecgan, to put something down.
items.cn: lay 来自古英语动词 lecgan，意为把东西放下。

items.en: Middle English used lay out for spreading things on a surface.
items.cn: 中古英语用 lay out 表示把东西摊开在平面上。

items.en: The phrasal verb lay out came to mean arranging a room, a page or a plan.
items.cn: 短语动词 lay out 逐渐表示布置房间、排版或规划。

items.en: In the nineteenth century the two words were joined into the noun layout.
items.cn: 十九世纪，这两个词合并成名词 layout。

items.en: Modern English uses layout for pages, rooms, factories and computer screens.
items.cn: 现代英语用 layout 指页面、房间、工厂和电脑屏幕的布局。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms of the phrasal verb and one compound with another meaning; the near-meaning group collects words for arrangement and design.
note.cn: 形近组收短语动词的各种形式和一个意义不同的复合词；近义组收表示安排与设计的词。

entries.definition: To spread something out or to arrange it according to a plan.
entries.definitionCN: 把东西摊开，或按计划加以布置。

entries.definition: Arranged or spread out in a particular way.
entries.definitionCN: 按某种方式布置好或摊开的。

entries.definition: An amount of money spent on something; the parts look alike but the meaning is different.
entries.definitionCN: 为某事花出的一笔钱；两个成分拼写相同，但词义不同。

entries.definition: A new or repeated arrangement of a page or space.
entries.definitionCN: 对页面或空间重新进行的布局。

entries.definition: The way things are put in order or in position.
entries.definitionCN: 事物被排成顺序或摆好位置的方式。

entries.definition: A plan or pattern made before something is built.
entries.definitionCN: 在建造之前拟定的计划或样式。

entries.definition: The arrangement of parts to form a whole, especially in art.
entries.definitionCN: 各部分组成整体的安排，尤用于艺术。

entries.definition: The shape, size and general arrangement of a page or file.
entries.definitionCN: 页面或文件的形状、尺寸与总体安排。

normalIntro.en: The word is a compound of a Germanic verb and a particle, and its senses all keep the idea of placing things into a plan.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由一个日耳曼语动词和一个副词小品词复合而成，各义项都保留「把东西放进计划」的想法。

normal.en: Lay out began as a verb meaning to spread things on a surface, and layout simply froze that action into a noun.
normal.cn: lay out 起初是动词，意为把东西摊在平面上，layout 则把这个动作凝固成名词。

normal.en: Page layout is the oldest noun sense: printers laid out type before they printed a sheet.
normal.cn: page layout 是最早的名词义：印刷者在印一张纸之前先摆放活字。

normal.en: Office layout and kitchen layout use the same idea on furniture and rooms instead of type and pictures.
normal.cn: office layout 和 kitchen layout 把同一想法用到家具和房间上，而不是字与图。

normal.en: A layout plan is the drawing of the arrangement, which is why the noun can also name a diagram.
normal.cn: layout plan 是布局的图纸，所以这个名词也能指一张图。

normal.en: Relayout adds re- to layout, so it means arranging the same space or page again.
normal.cn: relayout 在 layout 前加 re-，意为把同一空间或页面重新布置。

abstract.en: Layout is what turns a pile of things into a readable space, whether paper, room or factory.
abstract.cn: layout 把一堆东西变成可读的空间，无论是纸张、房间还是工厂。

abstract.en: The same word covers the act, the result and the drawing of an arrangement, because planning leaves all three behind.
abstract.cn: 同一个词覆盖动作、结果和图纸，因为规划会留下这三样东西。

abstract.en: A good layout is invisible: we notice it only when the parts refuse to fit.
abstract.cn: 好的布局是看不见的：只有当各部分配不上时，我们才会注意它。

examples.en: The designer changed the layout of the page to give the photos more room.
examples.cn: 设计师调整了页面布局，给照片留出更多空间。

examples.en: The new layout of the kitchen puts the sink under the window.
examples.cn: 厨房的新布局把水槽放到了窗下。

examples.en: The engineer handed us a layout of the factory floor.
examples.cn: 工程师递给我们一张车间平面布置图。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「累奥特」——设计师排完版面累得直说奥特；layout 是布局。

root: 由英语动词 lay（古英语 lecgan，放下）与副词 out 复合，十九世纪固化为名词 layout。

sensesIntro.en: The core is arrangement; the senses divide into page design, the arrangement of a space, and the drawing that records it.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是安排；义项由此分为页面设计、空间布置，以及记录安排方式的图纸。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: sheets of paper on a desk, with blocks and lines placed into clear positions.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌面上摊开的纸张，方块与线条被摆成清楚的位置关系。

branches.en: a page where photos and text find their places
branches.cn: 照片与文字各就其位的页面

branches.en: a print proof marked with arrows and boxes
branches.cn: 用箭头和方框标出的校样

branches.en: a room rearranged around one window
branches.cn: 围绕一扇窗重新布置的房间

branches.en: a factory plan spread on a table
branches.cn: 摊在桌上的工厂平面图

branches.en: a screen divided into panels and menus
branches.cn: 被分成面板与菜单的屏幕

intro.en: A Germanic verb plus an English particle form the compound, and re- plus a participle show how the word keeps growing.
intro.cn: 一个日耳曼语动词加一个英语小品词构成这个复合词，而 re- 与过去分词又显示它仍在生长。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.example: lay a sheet on the table

items.meaningCN: 构成短语名词的小品词

definition_zh: 懒惰的；慵懒的；懒洋洋的；马虎的
definition_en: unwilling to work or make effort, pleasantly relaxed, slow and without force, or done without care
core_image: 午后斜阳照进院子，一个人摊在躺椅上，手边的杯子够不着也不愿起身
scene: 午后的院子里，躺椅上的人伸手够了够杯子，又把手放下。It was a lazy afternoon, and nobody wanted to move.
sceneCN: 这里是「慵懒的、悠闲的」（第 2 个义项：轻松惬意、不费力的状态）；句意为那是一个慵懒的午后，没人愿意动。可辨识画面：斜阳、躺椅、手边的杯子。

pos.zh: 懒惰的；慵懒的；懒洋洋的；马虎的

derivatives.zh: 由 lazy 变 y 为 i 再加 -ly 构成，义为「懒洋洋地」
由 lazy 变 y 为 i 再加 -ness 构成，义为「懒惰」
由 lazy 与 bones 复合，义为「懒骨头」
一般认为由 lazy 逆构而成，义为「懒散地打发时间」

senses.title: Unwilling to work or make effort
senses.definition: not willing to work or to make any effort
senses.definitionCN: 不愿意工作或付出任何努力
senses.example: He is too lazy to wash his own cup.
senses.exampleCN: 他懒得连自己的杯子都不洗。
senses.why: The word probably came from a Low German term for weak or useless, so laziness began as a body that would not serve.
senses.whyCN: 这个词很可能来自低地德语中表示虚弱、无用的说法，所以懒惰最初是身体不肯出力。

senses.title: Pleasantly relaxed
senses.definition: relaxed and slow in a pleasant way, as of a warm afternoon
senses.definitionCN: 轻松而缓慢，令人愉快，如温暖的午后
senses.example: We spent a lazy afternoon by the river.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在河边度过了一个慵懒的午后。
senses.why: If a body refuses effort, the same word can describe a time when no effort is asked for, and the refusal turns into comfort.
senses.whyCN: 身体若不肯出力，同一个词也能形容一段不需要出力的时间，拒绝就变成了惬意。

senses.title: Slow and without force
senses.titleCN: 懒洋洋的；缓慢不用力的
senses.definition: moving or flowing slowly, without energy
senses.definitionCN: 动作或流动缓慢，不带力气
senses.example: A lazy smile spread across his face.
senses.exampleCN: 他脸上浮起懒洋洋的笑。
senses.why: The idea of withheld effort moves easily onto movements and sounds, so slow and soft things are called lazy too.
senses.whyCN: 「不肯出力」的想法很容易挪到动作与声音上，于是缓慢柔和的东西也被说成 lazy。

senses.title: Careless, done without proper effort
senses.definition: done without care or attention, as a lazy attempt
senses.definitionCN: 做事不细心、不用心，如敷衍的尝试
senses.example: The report was a lazy piece of work.
senses.exampleCN: 那份报告写得很敷衍。
senses.why: When effort is withheld from work that needs it, the word stops being pleasant and becomes a criticism of quality.
senses.whyCN: 当该出力的活被省了力气，这个词就不再惬意，而成了对质量的批评。

intro.en: This word has no known Old English form; it appears in the sixteenth century, probably from a Low German or Dutch term for weakness.
intro.cn: 这个词没有已知的古英语形态，十六世纪才出现，一般认为来自低地德语或荷兰语中表示虚弱说法。

items.en: No Old English form is known, so the path before the sixteenth century is uncertain.
items.cn: 没有已知的古英语形式，十六世纪之前的来路并不确定。

items.en: The word is first recorded in the sixteenth century, probably from a Low German or Dutch term for weak or useless.
items.cn: 这个词最早见于十六世纪，一般认为来自低地德语或荷兰语中表示虚弱、无用的说法。

items.en: English lazy appears first meaning disinclined to work, with the bodily sense of weakness still near.
items.cn: 英语 lazy 最初表示不愿干活，身体虚弱的意味还很近。

items.en: The pleasant sense of a relaxed time grows later, especially in phrases like a lazy afternoon.
items.cn: 「悠闲时光」的愉快义出现较晚，尤见于 a lazy afternoon 这类说法。

items.en: Modern English uses lazy for people, for comfortable slow time, and for work done without care.
items.cn: 现代英语用 lazy 形容人、形容舒适缓慢的时间，也形容不用心做出的活。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built on the same stem or a similar shape; the near-meaning group collects other words for idleness and slowness.
note.cn: 形近组收由同一词干构成的或形状相近的形式；近义组收其他表示懒散与迟缓的词。

entries.definition: To spend time doing very little, formed from lazy.
entries.definitionCN: 几乎什么也不做地打发时间，由 lazy 逆构而来。

entries.definition: In a slow, relaxed manner.
entries.definitionCN: 以缓慢放松的方式。

entries.definition: The quality of being unwilling to work.
entries.definitionCN: 不愿工作的性质。

entries.definition: Slightly misty, not clear to see.
entries.definitionCN: 略有雾、看不清楚；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Not working or not in use.
entries.definitionCN: 不工作或不使用的。

entries.definition: Disliking effort or activity.
entries.definitionCN: 厌恶出力或活动的。

entries.definition: Moving or reacting more slowly than usual.
entries.definitionCN: 移动或反应比平常慢的。

entries.definition: Without energy or enthusiasm.
entries.definitionCN: 没有精力或热情的。

normalIntro.en: With no native Old English shape, the word is held together by an uncertain foreign source and the English endings that grew on it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词没有土生的古英语形态，靠一个不确定的外来来源与长在它上面的英语词尾支撑起来。

normal.en: Lazy has no known Old English form; it appears in the sixteenth century, probably from Low German or Dutch.
normal.cn: lazy 没有已知的古英语形式，十六世纪才出现，一般认为来自低地德语或荷兰语。

normal.en: Laze is a back-formation: the shorter verb was cut from the longer adjective.
normal.cn: laze 是逆构词：较短的动词是从较长的形容词上切下来的。

normal.en: Lazily and laziness change y to i before the suffix, as happy becomes happily.
normal.cn: lazily 与 laziness 在加后缀前把 y 变 i，就像 happy 变 happily。

normal.en: Lazybones is lazy plus bones, a joking name for a person who will not move.
normal.cn: lazybones 是 lazy 加 bones，是给不肯动的人起的玩笑称呼。

normal.en: A lazy afternoon is pleasant, but a lazy attempt is a criticism of the work.
normal.cn: a lazy afternoon 是惬意的，而 a lazy attempt 是对工作的批评。

abstract.en: The word began as a body that would not serve and ended as a description of comfort, a shift in who is judging.
abstract.cn: 这个词从「不肯出力的身体」走到「舒适的描述」，变的是谁在评判。

abstract.en: Calling a person lazy is a moral judgement, while calling an afternoon lazy is a gift of permission.
abstract.cn: 说一个人 lazy 是道德评判，而说一个午后 lazy 是允许人放松。

abstract.en: English separates the refusal of work from the need for rest by tone rather than by word.
abstract.cn: 英语用语气而不是用词，把「拒绝干活」与「需要休息」区分开。

examples.en: He is too lazy to wash his own cup.
examples.cn: 他懒得连自己的杯子都不洗。

examples.en: We spent a lazy afternoon by the river.
examples.cn: 我们在河边度过了一个慵懒的午后。

examples.en: The report was a lazy piece of work.
examples.cn: 那份报告写得很敷衍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「累极」——懒到把累极的身体摊在椅子上，什么也不想做；记住 lazy 是懒惰的。

root: 来源不确定；一般认为来自低地德语或荷兰语中表示虚弱、无用的说法，十六世纪进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a body withholding effort; the senses then add pleasant slowness, slow movement, and work done without care.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一具不肯出力的身体；义项由此加上惬意的缓慢、动作的迟缓，以及不用心做出的活。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaching for a cup and giving up halfway.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手伸向杯子，伸到一半又放下。

branches.en: a cup left unwashed beside a chair
branches.cn: 椅子旁没洗的杯子

branches.en: a long warm afternoon with nobody moving
branches.cn: 漫长温暖、无人起身的午后

branches.en: a slow smile spreading without hurry
branches.cn: 不急不忙地铺开的笑

branches.en: a report finished in ten careless minutes
branches.cn: 十分钟草草写完的报告

branches.en: a body sunk deep into a deck chair
branches.cn: 深陷在躺椅里的身体

intro.en: This word has no native Old English shape, so its parts are the uncertain foreign source and the English endings that grew on it.
intro.cn: 这个词没有土生的古英语形态，它的构件是那个不确定的外来来源，以及长在它上面的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: No Latin cognate is recorded; the source is probably Low German or Dutch.
latinIntro.cn: 没有记录在案的拉丁同族词；来源很可能是低地德语或荷兰语。

items.meaningCN: 闲散度日，由 lazy 逆构

items.meaning: lazy plus bones, an idle person
items.meaningCN: lazy 与 bones 复合，指懒人

definition_zh: 领导；带领；导致；领先
definition_en: to guide or be in charge of others, to cause something to happen, or to be ahead
core_image: 一个人走在队伍最前面，身后的人跟着他选的方向
scene: 队伍在岔路口停下，向导抬手示意大家往左边走。She led the group through the narrow pass.
sceneCN: 这里是「带领、引导」（第 1 个义项：动词，指走在前头带路）；句意为她带着队伍穿过狭窄的山口。图中可辨识物件：岔路口、向导的手势、狭窄山口。

derivatives.zh: 由 lead 加 -er 构成，义为「领导者；领袖」
由 lead 加 -ing 构成，义为「领先的；主要的」
由 leader 加 -ship 构成，义为「领导；领导力」
由 mis-（错误地）加 lead 构成，义为「误导」

senses.title: To guide someone along a way
senses.definition: to go in front of others and show them the way
senses.definitionCN: 走在别人前面并为他们指路
senses.example: She led the group through the narrow pass.
senses.exampleCN: 她带着队伍穿过狭窄的山口。
senses.why: The Old English verb meant to cause someone to go; the leader is the one who sets the direction of that going.
senses.whyCN: 这个古英语动词本义是「使某人走」，带路的人就是决定「往哪走」的那个人。

senses.title: To be in charge of people or an activity
senses.definition: to direct a group, organization or activity and be responsible for it
senses.definitionCN: 指挥一个群体、组织或活动并对其负责
senses.example: He leads a team of twelve engineers.
senses.exampleCN: 他领导着一支十二名工程师的团队。
senses.why: From physically going first it is a short step to deciding for others, so lead comes to mean holding authority.
senses.whyCN: 从身体上走在最前，很容易走到「替别人做决定」，于是 lead 转而指掌握权力。

senses.title: To cause something to happen
senses.definition: to be the cause or route by which a result happens
senses.definitionCN: 成为某个结果发生的原因或路径
senses.example: Poor sleep can lead to serious health problems.
senses.exampleCN: 睡眠不足可能导致严重的健康问题。
senses.why: A path leads to a place; events also have paths, so lead to names the route by which one thing brings about another.
senses.whyCN: 一条路通向一个地方；事情也有路径，所以 lead to 指一件事带出另一件事的路线。

senses.title: To be ahead in a race or competition
senses.definition: to have more points or be further forward than others in a contest
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛中比别人得分多或位置更靠前
senses.example: Our team leads by two goals.
senses.exampleCN: 我们队领先两球。
senses.why: The one in front is literally leading the line, and the racing sense keeps that simple picture of position.
senses.whyCN: 走在最前的人字面上就在「带」着队伍，竞赛义保留了这个简单的方位画面。

senses.title: The position of being ahead
senses.definition: the first place or advantage held over others in a contest
senses.definitionCN: 在竞争中占据的第一名次或优势
senses.example: The champion held the lead until the final lap.
senses.exampleCN: 冠军一直保持领先直到最后一圈。
senses.why: The verb's sense of being in front turns into a noun naming that front position.
senses.whyCN: 动词「处在前面」的意思转成一个名词，指那个靠前的位置。

senses.title: A clue in an investigation
senses.definition: a piece of information that suggests where to look next
senses.definitionCN: 提示下一步该往哪里查的信息
senses.example: The police followed a new lead.
senses.exampleCN: 警方追查了一条新线索。
senses.why: A lead is something that leads you somewhere; in an investigation it is the information that pulls the search forward.
senses.whyCN: lead 是能把你带到某处的东西；在调查里，它就是推动搜查往前走的信息。

intro.en: Lead comes from an Old English verb meaning to cause to go, and it has kept the picture of someone walking in front.
intro.cn: lead 来自古英语中意为「使……走」的动词，一直保留着「有人走在前面」的画面。

items.en: Lædan meant to cause someone to go, to guide or to bring along a way.
items.cn: lædan 意为使某人走、引导或沿路带领。

items.en: The reconstructed verb *laidijan is related to the noun for a path or way.
items.cn: 重构动词 *laidijan 与表示「道路、路径」的名词有关。

items.en: Middle English leden keeps the sense of guiding and adds the idea of being first in a group.
items.cn: 中古英语 leden 保留引导义，并添上「在群体中最先」的意思。

items.en: The noun lead, meaning the first place, appears in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 表示第一名的名词 lead 在十五世纪出现。

items.en: Modern English adds lead to 'cause' and lead as a clue, while the metal lead is a different word with a different vowel.
items.cn: 现代英语添上 lead to（导致）与「线索」义；金属铅则是另一个词，元音也不同。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers inflections and relatives of the verb; the near-meaning group gathers words for guiding and being first.
note.cn: 形近组收动词的变形与同族词；近义组收表示引导与领先的词。

entries.definition: The past tense and past participle of lead.
entries.definitionCN: lead 的过去式与过去分词。

entries.definition: A person who leads a group.
entries.definitionCN: 领导者；领袖。

entries.definition: Most important or in first place.
entries.definitionCN: 领先的；主要的。

entries.definition: To guide someone in the wrong direction.
entries.definitionCN: 误导；把某人带错方向。

entries.definition: To show someone the way.
entries.definitionCN: 引导；带路。

entries.definition: To organize and carry out an activity.
entries.definitionCN: 组织；进行。

entries.definition: To control or manage an activity.
entries.definitionCN: 指挥；管理。

entries.definition: To be the leader of a group.
entries.definitionCN: 领导；作为……的首领。

normalIntro.en: The past tense led drops the a of the present, and the family shows how guiding, leading and causing are one motion.
normalIntro.cn: 过去式 led 去掉了现在式中的 a；词族显示引导、领导与导致是同一种运动。

normal.en: The past tense is led, not leaded: lead, led, led.
normal.cn: 过去式是 led，不是 leaded：lead、led、led。

normal.en: Leader adds -er: the one who leads.
normal.cn: leader 加 -er，指带路的人。

normal.en: Lead to means to cause a result, as a road leads to a town.
normal.cn: lead to 意为导致结果，就像路通向城镇。

normal.en: Take the lead means to move into first place.
normal.cn: take the lead 意为取得领先。

normal.en: The metal lead is spelled the same but pronounced /led/ and has a different origin.
normal.cn: 金属铅拼写相同但读 /led/，词源也不同。

abstract.en: A word for walking in front turns into a word for authority because direction is a kind of decision.
abstract.cn: 一个「走在前面」的词变成「权力」的词，因为方向本身就是一种决定。

abstract.en: Lead to shows that causation is imagined as a path with a destination.
abstract.cn: lead to 说明因果关系被想象成一条有终点的路。

abstract.en: A clue is called a lead because information, too, can point a way.
abstract.cn: 线索被称为 lead，因为信息也能指出一条路。

examples.en: She led the group through the narrow pass.
examples.cn: 她带着队伍穿过狭窄的山口。

examples.en: He leads a team of twelve engineers.
examples.cn: 他领导着一支十二名工程师的团队。

examples.en: Poor sleep can lead to serious health problems.
examples.cn: 睡眠不足可能导致严重的健康问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「立德」——走在前面立起德行，才能领导别人；lead 记作「领导」。

root: 古英语 lædan（使……走、引导），与表示「道路」的名词同源，属日耳曼语族。

sensesIntro.en: The core is walking in front; it extends from guiding a group to holding authority, causing results, being first, and pointing a search.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「走在前面」；由带路扩展到掌权、导致结果、处于领先，以及为调查指路。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one person at the front choosing a direction while the others follow.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人走在最前面选方向，其余人跟着走。

branches.en: a guide raising a hand at a fork
branches.cn: 在岔路口抬手的向导

branches.en: a manager setting the week's direction
branches.cn: 为这一周定方向的经理

branches.en: a road that ends at a hospital
branches.cn: 通向医院的路

branches.en: a runner a stride ahead of the field
branches.cn: 领先一步的跑者

branches.en: a note that sends a search down a new street
branches.cn: 把搜查引向新街道的纸条

intro.en: An Old English verb, its irregular past, and three suffixes carry the family; a prefix creates its opposite.
intro.cn: 一个古英语动词、它不规则的变化形式，以及三个后缀支撑词族；一个前缀造出反义词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 领导者；带头人；领先者；（英）社论；（钓鱼）前导线；乐团首席
definition_en: a person or thing that guides, directs or is ahead of others
core_image: 队伍最前面的人回头看了一眼，确认后面的人都还跟着，然后继续走
scene: 出发前，队伍最前面的人回头清点人数，确认没有人掉队才继续前进。The group chose a new leader before the season began.
sceneCN: 这里指「带领群体的那个人」（第 1 个义项：群体的领导者）；句意为赛季开始前，这个团体选出了一位新的领导者。可辨识物件：队伍、背包、路口、名册、手杖。

pos.zh: 领先者；领先企业或产品

derivatives.zh: 带领；领先；线索
领先的；主要的
领导；领导力；领导层
带领（过去式与过去分词）
误导
没有领导的

senses.title: The person who guides a group
senses.definition: a person who directs the movement or activity of a group and whom others follow
senses.definitionCN: 指引一个群体的行动或活动、并被他人跟随的人
senses.example: The group chose a new leader before the season began.
senses.exampleCN: 赛季开始前，这个团体选出了一位新的领导者。
senses.why: The verb means 'to cause to go', and the agent ending marks the one who does the causing.
senses.whyCN: 动词意为「使行走」，施事后缀标记的正是那个发出使动的人。

senses.title: The head of an organization or government
senses.definition: the person holding the highest office in a party, union, company or state
senses.definitionCN: 在政党、工会、公司或国家中占据最高职位的人
senses.example: Union leaders met the minister on Tuesday.
senses.exampleCN: 工会领袖们在周二会见了部长。
senses.why: A group large enough to have offices needs a person at the top of its chart, and that person is its leader.
senses.whyCN: 一个大到设有办公室的群体，需要在组织图顶端有一个人，这个人就是它的领导者。

senses.title: The one in front of a race
senses.definition: the competitor currently ahead of all others in a race or contest
senses.definitionCN: 在赛跑或竞赛中目前领先于所有其他人的人
senses.example: The leader pulled away on the final climb.
senses.exampleCN: 领先者在最后一段爬坡时拉开了距离。
senses.why: The same word covers physical position: whoever is furthest along the course is simply the one leading.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词也覆盖物理位置：在赛道上走得最远的人，自然就是领跑者。

senses.title: The top firm or product
senses.titleCN: 市场中最领先的企业或产品
senses.definition: the company or brand with the largest share or strongest position in a market
senses.definitionCN: 在市场中份额最大或地位最强的公司或品牌
senses.example: The company is the market leader in small turbines.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司是小型涡轮机市场的领先者。
senses.why: Markets are treated as races, so the firm furthest ahead carries the name of the runner in front.
senses.whyCN: 市场被当作赛跑，因此跑得最远的公司就带上了最前面那位选手的名称。

senses.title: A leading newspaper article
senses.definition: in British usage, the main editorial that states the paper's opinion
senses.definitionCN: 英式用法中指表明报纸立场的主要社论
senses.example: The newspaper's leader criticized the plan as too costly.
senses.exampleCN: 该报的社论批评这项计划代价过高。
senses.why: The article that stands at the head of the opinion page is literally the leading piece.
senses.whyCN: 站在评论版最前面的那篇文章，字面上就是「领头的」那篇。

senses.title: The line between fly and fish
senses.titleCN: 鱼线与假饵之间的前导线
senses.definition: in angling, the length of line attached between the main line and the hook or fly
senses.definitionCN: 钓鱼时连接主线与鱼钩或假饵的那段线
senses.example: He tied a longer leader to the fly line before casting.
senses.exampleCN: 抛竿之前，他在飞蝇线上接了一段更长的前导线。
senses.why: The leader goes in front of the main line and leads the fly to the fish, so angling borrowed the ordinary word.
senses.whyCN: 前导线走在主线之前，把假饵引向鱼，钓鱼术语因此借用了这个普通词。

senses.title: The first chair in an orchestra
senses.definition: the principal player, especially the first violinist, who leads the section and stands in for the conductor
senses.definitionCN: 主要演奏者，尤指首席小提琴手，负责带领声部并在需要时代行指挥
senses.example: The orchestra's leader tuned the strings before the overture.
senses.exampleCN: 乐团首席在序曲之前为弦乐调音。
senses.why: Music uses the word for the player who stands first and gives the cue to the section.
senses.whyCN: 音乐用这个词指站在最前面、向声部发出提示的演奏者。

senses.title: The person who takes a group up a mountain
senses.definition: a qualified person who guides a group along a route and takes responsibility for its safety
senses.definitionCN: 沿路线引导团队并对安全负责的合格人员
senses.example: The mountain leader checked every rope before the descent.
senses.exampleCN: 登山向导在下撤之前检查了每一根绳索。
senses.why: Guidance on a route is the oldest sense of leading: someone who knows the way walks in front.
senses.whyCN: 在路线上引导是「带领」最古老的义项：知道路的人走在前面。

intro.en: Leader is lead plus the agent ending -er. Lead comes from Old English lǣdan 'to lead, guide', a causative form related to līþan 'to go, travel'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: leader 由 lead 加施事后缀构成。lead 出自古英语 lǣdan「带领、引导」，是与 līþan「行走、旅行」相关的使役形式。年代均为约数。

items.en: Līþan meant 'to go, travel'. Its earlier Germanic source is reconstructed rather than directly attested.
items.cn: līþan 意为「行走、旅行」。它在日耳曼语中更早的来源属于重构，而非直接有据。

items.en: Lǣdan was the causative partner, meaning 'to make go, conduct, guide'.
items.cn: lǣdan 是对应的使役词，意为「使行走、引导、带领」。

items.en: The ending -er marks the doer. English had a native agent ending, later reinforced by French -ier from Latin -arius.
items.cn: 这个施事后缀标记动作的执行者。英语本有本土的施事后缀，后来受到法语中源自拉丁语的相应后缀加强。

items.en: Leader named the person who conducts others, and by the seventeenth century it also named the first person in a race.
items.cn: leader 指带领他人的人；到十七世纪，它也指赛跑中最前面的人。

items.en: Angling, music and journalism each gave the word a narrow use, from the line before the fly to the article before the editorial page.
items.cn: 钓鱼、音乐与新闻各自赋予这个词专门用法，从假饵之前的线，到评论版最前面的文章。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the pre-Germanic source of līþan is a reconstruction, and no exact first citation is fixed for the angling sense, so dates here are approximations.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：līþan 在日耳曼语之前的来源属于重构形式；钓鱼义也没有确切的最早书证，因此这里给出的年代均为约数。

note.en: Group one holds the same guiding family; group two holds nouns for the person at the head of a group.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「引导」词族的词；第二组是表示群体首位者的名词。

entries.definition: To guide or be first; the person noun is built directly on this verb.
entries.definitionCN: 引导或处于首位；这个表示人的名词直接由该动词构成。

entries.definition: Means guiding or ahead; it describes the position rather than the person.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「引导的」或「领先的」；描述位置，而非人。

entries.definition: The ability, position or body of leaders; it surrounds the person with a role.
entries.definitionCN: 领导能力、职位或领导层；它把这个人包在一个角色里。

entries.definition: To guide in the wrong direction; it shares the walking root but reverses the purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 把人引向错误方向；共享「行走」词根，却把目的反转。

entries.definition: The person in charge of an organization; it stresses office more than the act of guiding.
entries.definitionCN: 一个组织的主管者；强调职位，而非引导的动作。

entries.definition: The highest-ranking person in a body, often in a traditional or official title.
entries.definitionCN: 某个机构中地位最高的人，常用于传统或官方头衔。

entries.definition: A person who opens a new field or route; a leader can follow an existing path, a pioneer cannot.
entries.definitionCN: 开辟新领域或新路线的人；领导者可以走已有的路，先驱则不能。

entries.definition: The competitor thought most likely to win; it is close to the race sense of leader.
entries.definitionCN: 被认为最可能获胜的竞争者；接近 leader 的赛跑义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real walking root, the real agent ending and the real institutional phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「行走」词根、真实的施事后缀与真实的机构搭配。

normal.en: The verb means 'to cause to go', and the ending means 'the one who', so a leader is the one who makes others go.
normal.cn: 动词意为「使行走」，后缀意为「……的人」，因此领导者就是使他人前进的人。

normal.en: The family runs lead, leader, leading, led, leadership, mislead and leaderless.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 lead、leader、leading、led、leadership、mislead 与 leaderless。

normal.en: The organizational phrases are team leader, world leader and leader of the opposition.
normal.cn: 组织搭配有团队负责人、世界领导人与反对党领袖。

normal.en: The market phrase is market leader, and the everyday phrase is follow the leader.
normal.cn: 市场搭配是市场领先者，日常说法是跟着领头的人做。

normal.en: The same root appears in mislead, where the guiding is deliberately wrong.
normal.cn: 同一词根出现在 mislead 中，那里的引导是故意走错方向。

abstract.en: Picture someone at the front of a column who turns back to count the walkers.
abstract.cn: 想象队伍最前面的人回头清点人数。

abstract.en: Picture a runner whose back is the only thing the others can see.
abstract.cn: 想象一名跑者，其他人只看得见他的背影。

abstract.en: Picture a first violinist raising the bow so that an entire section know when to begin.
abstract.cn: 想象首席小提琴手举起弓，让整个声部知道何时开始。

examples.en: A good leader makes the next decision easier for everyone else.
examples.cn: 好的领导者会让其他人做下一个决定时更容易。

examples.en: The market leader cut prices before the smaller firms could respond.
examples.cn: 市场领先者在较小公司来得及反应之前就降了价。

examples.en: The newspaper's leader called for an independent inquiry.
examples.cn: 该报的社论要求进行独立调查。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「带领」加「人」——走在最前、让别人跟着走的那个人 → 领导者、领先者

root: leader 由 lead 加施事后缀构成。lead 出自古英语 lǣdan「带领」，与 līþan「行走」相关的使役形式；这个后缀标记执行者。更早的日耳曼来源属于重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one figure: the one who goes first. The figure is a guide of people, a head of an institution, a runner in front, a top firm, a leading article, a line ahead of the fly, a first violinist and a mountain guide.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个人物展开：走在最前面的那一个。这个人物依次是人群的引导者、机构首脑、跑在前面的选手、顶尖企业、头篇评论、假饵前的线、首席小提琴手与登山向导。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the walker at the front who turns to check the column.
core.cn: 核心意象：走在最前面、回头清点队伍的人。

branches.en: THE GUIDE: whether on a trail or in a meeting, the leader is the one who knows the way and walks ahead.
branches.cn: 向导：无论在林间小径上还是在会议中，领导者都是识路并走在前面的人。

branches.en: THE OFFICE: a large body needs a person at the top of its chart.
branches.cn: 职位：庞大的机构需要在组织图顶端有一个人。

branches.en: THE FRONT: a race and a market both measure who is furthest ahead.
branches.cn: 最前：赛跑与市场都在衡量谁跑得最远。

branches.en: THE LEADING WORD: the article at the head of the opinion page speaks for the paper.
branches.cn: 领头之言：评论版最前面的文章代表报纸发言。

branches.en: THE FIRST IN LINE: a fishing trace and a first violin both stand ahead of the rest.
branches.cn: 队列之首：钓鱼前导线与首席小提琴都站在其余之前。

intro.en: The noun can be read from an Old English verb of going, its causative partner and the agent ending that marks the doer.
intro.cn: 这个名词可以按表示行走的古英语动词、它的使役对应词以及标记执行者的施事后缀逐段读出。

latinIntro.en: This word is native English rather than Latin: the Germanic walking root supplies the verb, and the agent ending marks the person.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是英语本族词而非拉丁借词：日耳曼语中表示行走的词根提供动词，施事后缀标记人。

items.example: The old verb named ordinary movement.
items.exampleCN: 这个古动词指普通移动。

items.example: The causative verb added the idea of conducting others.
items.exampleCN: 这个使役动词增添了带领他人的意思。

items.example: He led the team through the gate.
The ending marks the person who performs the action.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标记执行动作的人。

items.example: The leader waited at the fork in the path.
The leading car turned off the highway.
items.exampleCN: 领头的那辆车驶离了公路。

items.example: She led the group down the ridge.
The team turned to her for leadership.
A false sign misled the hikers.
items.exampleCN: 一块错误的牌子误导了徒步者。
这个没有领导的群体逐渐散开。

definition_zh: 领导；领导能力；领导层；领导地位
definition_en: the ability or activity of guiding a group, or the people who hold that role
core_image: 队伍最前面的人举着火把，后面的人跟着那点光走，暗处的路看不清
scene: 夜路上，走在最前面的人举着火把，后面的人跟着那点光前进。Her leadership turned a divided committee into a working team.
sceneCN: 这里指「带领群体行动的领导能力」（第 1 个义项：引导群体的能力）；句意为她的领导力把一个分裂的委员会变成了能运转的团队。可辨识物件：火把、夜路、队伍、前方拐角、脚印。

pos.zh: 领导；领导能力（常作不可数）
领导层；领导班子（集合名词）

collocations.zh: 思想领导力；行业思想权威

forms.label: 可数用法（领导层，少见复数）

derivatives.zh: 领导者；领先者
带领；领先；线索
领先的；主要的
带领（过去式与过去分词）
误导（同出「行走」词根）
没有领导的

senses.title: The ability to guide a group
senses.definition: the capacity to set a direction and keep a group working toward it
senses.definitionCN: 确定方向并使一个群体朝该方向持续行动的能力
senses.example: Her leadership turned a divided committee into a working team.
senses.exampleCN: 她的领导力把一个分裂的委员会变成了能运转的团队。
senses.why: The verb behind the word means 'to cause to go'; leadership is the ability to make a group go in one direction.
senses.whyCN: 这个词背后的动词意为「使行走」；领导力就是使一个群体朝同一方向前进的能力。

senses.title: The position of leader
senses.definition: the office or role of being the person who directs a group
senses.definitionCN: 指导一个群体的那个人所占据的职位或角色
senses.example: He assumed leadership of the party after the election.
senses.exampleCN: 选举之后，他接任了该党的领导职务。
senses.why: The suffix turns a person into a state: being a leader is a role that can be entered and left.
senses.whyCN: 后缀把人变成一种状态：做领导者是一个可以进入也可以离开的角色。

senses.title: The group at the top
senses.definition: the collective body of people who hold the highest directing roles in an organization
senses.definitionCN: 在一个组织中占据最高指导职位的集体
senses.example: The leadership met behind closed doors before the vote.
senses.exampleCN: 投票之前，领导层闭门开会。
senses.why: English often treats a set of office-holders as one collective noun, so the role becomes a body.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把一群任职者当作一个集合名词，于是职位变成了一个机构。

senses.title: A way of leading
senses.definition: a characteristic manner of directing others, such as coaching, directing or delegating
senses.definitionCN: 指导他人的典型方式，如教练式、指挥式或授权式
senses.example: A coaching style of leadership improved staff retention.
senses.exampleCN: 教练式的领导风格提高了员工留任率。
senses.why: Once leadership is studied, its manners are classified, and each one becomes a named style.
senses.whyCN: 一旦领导被研究，它的做法就会被分类，每一种做法都成为一个有名称的风格。

senses.title: Direction at the level of government
senses.definition: the activity of setting public direction and taking responsibility for national or local decisions
senses.definitionCN: 确定公共方向并为国家或地方决策承担责任的活动
senses.example: Political leadership was slow to recognize the drought.
senses.exampleCN: 政治领导层迟迟没有认识到旱情的严重。
senses.why: The word moves easily from a team to a state, because both need someone to set a course.
senses.whyCN: 这个词很容易从团队移到国家，因为两者都需要有人确定航向。

senses.title: Authority of ideas in an industry
senses.definition: the reputation of shaping how an industry thinks, often built through research and public comment
senses.definitionCN: 塑造一个行业思考方式的声誉，常通过研究与公开发言建立
senses.example: The firm publishes reports to establish thought leadership in the field.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司发布报告，以在该领域建立思想领导力。
senses.why: Leading need not mean commanding; whoever defines the questions can lead an industry's attention.
senses.whyCN: 领导不必意味着命令；能界定问题的人就能引导一个行业的注意力。

senses.title: First place in a market
senses.definition: the position of having the largest share or the strongest reputation in a market
senses.definitionCN: 在市场中获得最大份额或最强声誉的位置
senses.example: The brand lost market leadership after the recall.
senses.exampleCN: 召回事件之后，这个品牌失去了市场领先地位。
senses.why: Competition borrows the image of a race: the leader is simply the one furthest ahead.
senses.whyCN: 竞争借用了赛跑的意象：领先者就是跑在最前面的那一个。

senses.title: Keeping a group together in difficulty
senses.titleCN: 困境中维持群体的凝聚
senses.definition: the work of holding a group together and making it continue when conditions are hard
senses.definitionCN: 在艰难条件下维持群体并使其继续前进的工作
senses.example: Leadership in a storm means keeping the group together, not walking fastest.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴中的领导意味着让队伍保持在一起，而不是自己走得最快。
senses.why: The oldest image is a person walking ahead with a light; the point is not speed but that others can still follow.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意象是一个人举着光走在前面；重点不是速度，而是后来的人仍能跟上。

intro.en: Leadership joins leader with the noun suffix -ship. Leader comes from the verb lead, from Old English lǣdan 'to lead, guide', a causative form related to līþan 'to go, travel'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: leadership 由 leader 加名词后缀构成。leader 来自动词 lead，后者出自古英语 lǣdan「带领、引导」，是与 līþan「行走、旅行」相关的使役形式。年代均为约数。

items.en: Līþan meant 'to go, travel'. Its earlier Germanic source is reconstructed rather than directly attested.
items.cn: līþan 意为「行走、旅行」。它在日耳曼语中更早的来源属于重构，而非直接有据。

items.en: Lǣdan was the causative partner of līþan, meaning 'to make go, conduct, guide'.
items.cn: lǣdan 是 līþan 的使役对应词，意为「使行走、引导、带领」。

items.en: The verb lead survived into Middle English and extended from guiding people to being first in a race or market.
items.cn: 动词 lead 进入中古英语，并从引导人扩展到在竞赛或市场中领先。

items.en: Leader named the person who conducts others, formed from the verb with an agent ending.
items.cn: leader 指带领他人的人，由动词加施事后缀构成。

items.en: The ending -ship comes from Old English -scipe, meaning 'state or condition', so leadership is the state of being a leader.
items.cn: 这个名词后缀来自古英语中表示「状态或境况」的相应后缀，因此 leadership 就是身为领导者的状态。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the pre-Germanic source of līþan is a reconstruction, and no exact first citation is fixed for the modern managerial sense, so dates here are approximations.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：līþan 在日耳曼语之前的来源属于重构形式；现代管理义也没有确切的最早书证，因此这里给出的年代均为约数。

note.en: Group one holds the same guiding family in other grammatical roles; group two holds nouns for directing people and work.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「引导」词族、语法角色不同的词；第二组是指挥人与工作的名词。

entries.definition: The person who guides a group; leadership is the role, ability or body that surrounds that person.
entries.definitionCN: 引导群体的人；leadership 是围绕这个人的角色、能力或集体。

entries.definition: To guide or be first; it names the action from which the noun is built.
entries.definitionCN: 引导或处于首位；它指构成这个名词的动作。

entries.definition: Means guiding or being ahead; as an adjective it describes the front position.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「引导的」或「领先的」；作形容词时描述最前的位置。

entries.definition: To guide someone in the wrong direction; it shares the same walking root but adds a prefix of error.
entries.definitionCN: 把人引向错误方向；共享同一个「行走」词根，只是加上表示错误的前缀。

entries.definition: The activity of planning and controlling resources; leadership sets direction, management maintains the system.
entries.definitionCN: 计划与控制资源的活动；领导确定方向，管理维持系统。

entries.definition: Advice or direction given to someone who needs to find a path; it is usually less formal than leadership.
entries.definitionCN: 给需要找路的人以建议或方向；通常比 leadership 更不正式。

entries.definition: The course or line along which something moves; leadership is the act of setting that course.
entries.definitionCN: 某物前进的路线或方向；leadership 是设定这条路线的行为。

entries.definition: Recognized power to command; a leader may have authority, but leadership can exist without it.
entries.definitionCN: 被承认的命令权；领导者可以拥有权威，但领导力也能在没有权威时存在。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real walking root, the real suffix and the real organizational phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「行走」词根、真实的后缀与真实的组织搭配。

normal.en: The verb means 'to cause to go', so leadership is the ability to make a group go forward together.
normal.cn: 动词意为「使行走」，因此领导力就是使一个群体共同前进的能力。

normal.en: The suffix means 'state or condition', so leadership is literally the state of being a leader.
normal.cn: 后缀意为「状态或境况」，因此 leadership 字面上就是身为领导者的状态。

normal.en: The family runs lead, leader, leading, led, leadership and mislead.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 lead、leader、leading、led、leadership 与 mislead。

normal.en: The organizational phrases are under the leadership of, strong leadership and leadership style.
normal.cn: 组织搭配有在……的领导下、强有力的领导与领导风格。

normal.en: The political and business phrases are party leadership, market leadership and thought leadership.
normal.cn: 政治与商业搭配有党的领导层、市场领先地位与思想领导力。

abstract.en: Picture a torch at the front of a night column, visible just far enough to follow.
abstract.cn: 想象夜行队伍最前面的一支火把，光刚好够后面的人跟着走。

abstract.en: Picture a committee split into two rooms until one person brings both back to the same table.
abstract.cn: 想象一个委员会分裂在两个房间，直到有人把双方带回同一张桌子。

abstract.en: Picture a storm where the slowest walker sets the pace and no one is left behind.
abstract.cn: 想象一场风暴，最慢的人决定速度，没有人被落下。

examples.en: The school needs stable leadership before it can change the curriculum.
examples.cn: 学校需要稳定的领导层，才能改变课程。

examples.en: She studied leadership in small teams rather than in large corporations.
examples.cn: 她研究的是小团队中的领导，而非大公司中的领导。

examples.en: Under his leadership, the clinic doubled the number of patients it could see.
examples.cn: 在他的领导下，诊所能够接诊的病人数量翻了一倍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「带领」加「身份状态」——走在最前面并让后面的人跟上来 → 领导、领导力

root: leadership 由 leader 加名词后缀构成。leader 来自动词 lead，出自古英语 lǣdan「带领」，与 līþan「行走」相关的使役形式；这个名词后缀来自古英语中表示「状态」的相应后缀。更早的日耳曼来源属于重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one image: someone walks in front with a light. The image becomes an ability, a position, a body of leaders, a manner, a government's direction, an industry's authority, a market's first place and finally the work of keeping a group together in a storm.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个意象展开：有人举着光走在前面。这个意象依次变成能力、职位、领导班子、方式、政府的方向、行业的思想权威、市场的首位，最后是在风暴中维持群体不散的工作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a torch carried at the head of a night column.
core.cn: 核心意象：夜行队伍最前面的一支火把。

branches.en: THE ABILITY: the first sense is the capacity to set a direction and keep others moving.
branches.cn: 能力：第一个义项是确定方向并使他人持续前进的能力。

branches.en: THE ROLE AND THE STORM: holding the office and holding the group together are two sides of the same walk.
branches.cn: 职位与风暴：占据职位与维持群体不散，是同一次行走的两面。

branches.en: THE BODY: a set of office-holders becomes a collective noun with its own meetings.
branches.cn: 集体：一群任职者变成一个拥有自己会议的集合名词。

branches.en: THE MANNER AND THE MIND: coaching a team and shaping an industry's questions are both ways of leading.
branches.cn: 方式与思想：教练一个团队与塑造一个行业的问题，都是领导的方式。

branches.en: THE PUBLIC RACE: a government sets a national course, and a brand runs first in its market.
branches.cn: 公共赛跑：政府确定国家航向，品牌在其市场中跑在最前。

intro.en: The noun can be read from an Old English verb of going, its causative partner, an agent noun and the suffix of state.
intro.cn: 这个名词可以按表示行走的古英语动词、它的使役对应词、施事名词以及表示状态的后缀逐段读出。

latinIntro.en: This word is native English rather than Latin: the Germanic walking root supplies lead, leader and leadership, and the state suffix comes from Old English.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是英语本族词而非拉丁借词：日耳曼语中表示行走的词根衍生 lead、leader 与 leadership，表示状态的后缀来自古英语。

items.example: The old verb named ordinary movement.
items.exampleCN: 这个古动词指普通的移动。

items.example: The causative verb added the idea of causing others to move.
items.exampleCN: 这个使役动词增添了使他人移动的意思。

items.example: She led the group through the pass.
The leader set the pace for the climb.
The leading runner never looked back.
items.exampleCN: 跑在最前面的选手从未回头。

items.example: The guide led us to the ridge.

items.meaning: the state or activity of leading
items.example: The team needed leadership after the loss.
items.exampleCN: 失利之后，这个团队需要领导。

items.example: The suffix turns a person into a role.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把一个人变成一种角色。

items.meaning: to guide in the wrong direction
items.example: The sign misled drivers into the closed road.
items.exampleCN: 那块牌子把司机引进了封闭的道路。

scene: 树枝上，一片叶子被风吹得翻了个面，露出浅色的背面。A leaf fell from the tree.

definition_zh: 联赛；联盟；同盟；（旧）结盟
definition_en: a group of sports teams that compete against one another, an alliance of states or groups, and an older verb meaning to unite in such an alliance
core_image: 一排球队队旗插在同一块场地上，旗与旗之间用绳子系在一起
scene: 赛季开始前，球迷在球场外排起长队。Their team finished top of the league last season.
sceneCN: 这里 league 指「联赛」（第 1 个义项）；句意为他们的球队上赛季排名联赛榜首。图中可辨识物件：队旗、球场看台、积分榜。

derivatives.zh: 由 league 与 table 复合，指联赛积分榜
由 non- 加 league 构成，指不属于职业联赛的
league 的复数形式，也可指很远的距离，如 leagues away

senses.title: A group of teams competing against each other
senses.definition: an organized group of sports clubs or teams that play against one another for a title
senses.definitionCN: 为争夺冠军而相互比赛的有组织的体育俱乐部或队伍
senses.example: Their team finished top of the league last season.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的球队上赛季排名联赛榜首。
senses.why: A league was first a group bound by an agreement, and teams bound into a fixture list are exactly that: a set of rivals tied to the same schedule.
senses.whyCN: league 最初指由协议绑在一起的一群人，而被赛程绑在一起的球队正是如此：一群被同一张日程拴住的对手。

senses.title: An alliance of states or groups
senses.definition: an association of countries, parties or groups formed to act together
senses.definitionCN: 为共同行动而组成的国家、政党或团体联合体
senses.example: Several small states formed a league to protect their trade routes.
senses.exampleCN: 几个小国结成联盟以保护各自的贸易路线。
senses.why: Latin ligare means to bind, so the political sense is the literal one: separate parties tied by a treaty into one body.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ligare 意为捆绑，所以政治义才是字面义：彼此独立的各方被条约绑成一个整体。

senses.title: To unite in an alliance
senses.definition: to join together with others in an alliance, now mainly literary or historical
senses.definitionCN: 与他人联合结成同盟，现在多用于文学或历史叙述
senses.example: The border towns leagued together against the raiders.
senses.exampleCN: 边境各镇联合起来对抗入侵者。
senses.why: If a league is a body bound together, then to league is simply to enter that binding, which is why the verb mirrors the noun.
senses.whyCN: 如果 league 是被绑在一起的整体，那么 to league 就是加入这次捆绑，因此动词与名词完全对应。

intro.en: League comes from a Latin verb meaning to bind, by way of Italian and French, so an alliance is literally a tying together.
intro.cn: league 经意大利语和法语来自拉丁语中意为「捆绑」的动词，所以同盟字面上就是「绑在一起」。

items.en: Ligare meant to bind or tie, and a league was first a binding together of people.
items.cn: ligare 意为捆绑、结合，而 league 最初指把人们绑在一起。

items.en: Italian lega named an alliance, a group bound by an agreement.
items.cn: 意大利语 lega 指同盟，即由协议绑在一起的一群人。

items.en: Old French ligue carried the political sense of a confederacy into English.
items.cn: 古法语 ligue 把「邦联、同盟」这一政治含义带进英语。

items.en: Middle English league named an alliance of rulers, and by the sixteenth century it also named a group of sports sides.
items.cn: 中古英语 league 指统治者之间的同盟，到十六世纪也指一组体育队伍。

items.en: Modern English keeps the alliance sense in phrases such as in league with, while the sports sense dominates everyday use.
items.cn: 现代英语在 in league with 等说法中保留同盟义，体育运动义则主导日常使用。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms and compounds of league; the near-meaning group collects other words for an alliance.
note.cn: 形近组收 league 的形式与复合词；近义组收其他表示同盟的词。

entries.definition: The plural of league, for several competitions or alliances.
entries.definitionCN: league 的复数，指多个联赛或同盟。

entries.definition: The past form, meaning formed an alliance.
entries.definitionCN: 过去式，意为结成了同盟。

entries.definition: Outside the professional league system, used of smaller clubs.
entries.definitionCN: 不属于职业联赛体系的，用于较小的俱乐部。

entries.definition: A formal agreement to work together.
entries.definitionCN: 正式约定共同行动的联盟。

entries.definition: A temporary union of parties or groups.
entries.definitionCN: 政党或团体组成的临时联合。

entries.definition: A union of states or organizations with shared rules.
entries.definitionCN: 按共同规则组成的国家或组织联合体。

entries.definition: The act or state of being joined together.
entries.definitionCN: 联合的行为或状态。

normalIntro.en: The word means a binding, and both a treaty and a fixture list are ways of tying separate parties into one arrangement.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词的意思是「捆绑」，而条约与赛程都是把彼此独立的一方绑进同一安排的方式。

normal.en: Latin ligare means to bind, so a league is people or teams tied together.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 ligare 意为捆绑，所以 league 就是被绑在一起的人或球队。

normal.en: The League of Nations was literally a binding of states after a war.
normal.cn: 国际联盟字面上就是战后各国的一次捆绑。

normal.en: In league with somebody usually hints at a secret or dishonest binding.
normal.cn: in league with somebody 通常暗示一种秘密或不正当的勾结。

normal.en: A football league is a binding by schedule: every club must play every other.
normal.cn: 足球联赛是一种按赛程的捆绑：每个俱乐部都必须与其他俱乐部比赛。

normal.en: To league is the old verb for entering that alliance, now mostly literary.
normal.cn: to league 是表示加入同盟的旧动词，现在多用于文学。

abstract.en: Competition and alliance share one word because both require parties to accept the same set of obligations.
abstract.cn: 竞争与同盟共用一个词，因为两者都要求各方接受同一套义务。

abstract.en: A league is a promise made visible: the table, the fixture list, the treaty are its rope.
abstract.cn: 联赛是把承诺变得可见：积分榜、赛程、条约就是它的绳子。

abstract.en: To be in league is to be tied to someone, whether by trust or by guilt.
abstract.cn: 身处一个 league 就是与某人绑在一起，不论靠信任还是靠罪责。

examples.en: Their team finished top of the league last season.
examples.cn: 他们的球队上赛季排名联赛榜首。

examples.en: Several small states formed a league to protect their trade routes.
examples.cn: 几个小国结成联盟以保护各自的贸易路线。

examples.en: The border towns leagued together against the raiders.
examples.cn: 边境各镇联合起来对抗入侵者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「离格」——离了格的球队被编进同一个联赛；谐音记住 league 是联赛、联盟。

root: 源自拉丁语 ligare（捆绑），经意大利语 lega 与古法语 ligue 进入英语；同盟本义即「绑在一起」。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a binding of separate parties; it appears as a political alliance, a sporting competition and the old verb for joining one.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是把彼此独立的各方绑在一起；它表现为政治同盟、体育联赛，以及表示加入同盟的旧动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: club flags planted in one field, tied to each other with rope.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排队旗插在同一块场地上，旗与旗用绳子系在一起。

branches.en: envoys signing a treaty in a plain room
branches.cn: 使节在简朴的房间里签署条约

branches.en: small states joining to guard a trade road
branches.cn: 小国联合以守护贸易通道

branches.en: a table showing every club's points
branches.cn: 显示各俱乐部积分的积分榜

branches.en: a full stadium on a match day
branches.cn: 比赛日坐满的球场

branches.en: border towns swearing to stand together
branches.cn: 边境各镇宣誓共同抵御

intro.en: A Latin verb for binding passes through Italian and French, and English adds plural and compound forms to name competitions and alliances.
intro.cn: 一个表示捆绑的拉丁动词经意大利语与法语传来，英语又加复数与复合形式来命名联赛与同盟。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 漏；漏出；漏洞；泄露（秘密）
definition_en: to let liquid or gas escape through a hole; to give out secret information; a hole through which something escapes, or the information disclosed
core_image: 水管接缝处慢慢渗出的一滴水珠
scene: 厨房水管接头处渗出水来，地上很快积了一小片。A small hole in the pipe let water leak into the basement.
sceneCN: 这里是「漏出」（第 1 个义项：液体从孔洞中漏出）；句意是管子上的小孔让水漏进了地下室。图中可辨识物件：水管接头、水珠、地面的水迹。

derivatives.zh: 由 leak 加 -age 构成，义为「泄漏；泄漏量」
由 leak 加 -y 构成，义为「漏的；爱泄露的」
由 leak 加 -er 构成，义为「泄密者」

senses.title: To let liquid or gas escape
senses.definition: to let liquid or gas escape through a hole or crack
senses.definitionCN: 让液体或气体从孔洞、裂缝中跑出来
senses.example: A small hole in the pipe let water leak into the basement.
senses.exampleCN: 管子上的小孔让水漏进了地下室。
senses.why: The Middle English verb named a slow dripping escape, so the physical movement of liquid is the oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 中古英语的动词指缓慢滴漏地跑掉，所以液体实际的移动是最早的义项。

senses.title: A hole through which something escapes
senses.definition: a hole or crack through which liquid or gas escapes
senses.definitionCN: 液体或气体借以跑出的孔洞或裂缝
senses.example: The plumber finally found the leak behind the sink.
senses.exampleCN: 水管工终于在水槽后面找到了漏洞。
senses.why: If a thing leaks, the opening that allows the escape can take the same name, turning the action into the place where it happens.
senses.whyCN: 某物会漏，那么允许它跑出的开口也能用同一个名字，于是动作变成了动作发生的位置。

senses.title: To give out secret information
senses.definition: to give secret information to someone who should not have it
senses.definitionCN: 把秘密信息交给不该得到它的人
senses.example: Someone leaked the report to the press before it was published.
senses.exampleCN: 有人在报告发表前把它泄露给了媒体。
senses.why: Information escapes like liquid: once the barrier is broken, what was contained spreads beyond its intended boundary.
senses.whyCN: 信息像液体一样跑掉：一旦屏障破了，原本被盛住的东西就会扩散到不该去的地方。

senses.title: The secret information disclosed
senses.definition: the secret information that has been disclosed
senses.definitionCN: 被泄露出去的秘密信息
senses.example: The leak forced the minister to explain himself in public.
senses.exampleCN: 泄露的消息迫使部长公开作出解释。
senses.why: By the same shift as the hole, the noun can name the disclosed material rather than the act of disclosing it.
senses.whyCN: 和「漏洞」一样的转喻，名词可以指被泄露的内容，而不是泄露这个动作。

intro.en: Leak is a Germanic word of uncertain exact origin, probably related to Dutch and Norse verbs for dripping; English extended it from water to secrets.
intro.cn: leak 是日耳曼语词，确切来源不确定，很可能与荷兰语、古诺斯语中表示滴落的动词有关；英语把它从水扩展到秘密。

items.en: A Germanic source is generally assumed, but the exact reconstructed form is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为源自日耳曼语，但确切的重构形式并不确定。

items.en: Middle Dutch leken meant to drip or to let liquid through.
items.cn: 中古荷兰语 leken 意为滴下或让液体透过。

items.en: Old Norse leka carried a similar sense of running or dripping.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 leka 有相近的「流淌、滴落」之意。

items.en: Middle English leken named the slow escape of liquid from a container.
items.cn: 中古英语 leken 指液体从容器中慢慢漏出。

items.en: Modern English extended the verb to secrets, and made the noun mean both the hole and the disclosure.
items.cn: 现代英语把动词扩展到秘密，并让名词同时指漏洞与泄露的内容。

note.en: The look-alike group collects derivatives and one homophone; the near-meaning group collects verbs of liquid and secrets escaping.
note.cn: 形近组收派生词和一个同音词；近义组收表示液体或秘密跑掉的动词。

entries.definition: The act of leaking, or the amount that escapes.
entries.definitionCN: 泄漏；泄漏的量。

entries.definition: Letting liquid through; not watertight.
entries.definitionCN: 会漏的；不密封的。

entries.definition: A person who gives secret information to others.
entries.definitionCN: 向他人泄露秘密的人。

entries.definition: A long green vegetable related to the onion; it sounds the same but has a different history.
entries.definitionCN: 一种与洋葱近亲的长绿蔬菜；它与 leak 同音，但词源不同。

entries.definition: To fall in small drops, usually slowly.
entries.definitionCN: 以小滴形式缓慢落下。

entries.definition: To let liquid flow out of a container by accident.
entries.definitionCN: 意外让液体从容器中流出。

entries.definition: To get out of a place where something is held.
entries.definitionCN: 从被盛放或困住的地方跑出来。

entries.definition: To make secret information known.
entries.definitionCN: 使秘密信息为人所知。

normalIntro.en: The word starts with liquid finding a way out; its suffixes build the amount, the quality and the person, and one homophone is a vegetable.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从液体找到出口开始；它的后缀造出量、性质和人物，而一个同音词是蔬菜。

normal.en: Leak began with liquid escaping through a small opening, which is why every later sense keeps the idea of a breach.
normal.cn: leak 起初指液体从小口跑出，所以后来每个义项都保留「破口」的想法。

normal.en: Leakage adds -age and names the process or the amount, not the hole itself.
normal.cn: leakage 加 -age，指过程或数量，而不是孔洞本身。

normal.en: Leaky adds -y and turns the verb into an adjective: a leaky bucket is one that lets water through.
normal.cn: leaky 加 -y，把动词变成形容词：leaky bucket 就是会漏水的水桶。

normal.en: Leaker adds -er and names the person who lets information out.
normal.cn: leaker 加 -er，指把信息放出去的人。

normal.en: Leek is only a homophone: the vegetable's name has a different origin and nothing to do with dripping.
normal.cn: leek 只是同音词：这种蔬菜的名字来源不同，与滴漏无关。

abstract.en: Containers fail at their edges, and so do institutions, which is why a word for a hole serves for a secret.
abstract.cn: 容器常在边缘失效，机构也是如此，所以一个表示孔洞的词能用来指秘密。

abstract.en: What leaks is always something that was meant to stay inside, so the word carries a quiet accusation.
abstract.cn: 漏出的东西总是本该留在里面的东西，所以这个词带着一种安静的指责。

abstract.en: A single drop is enough to prove the barrier has failed, which is why leaks are found before they are measured.
abstract.cn: 一滴就足以证明屏障已经失效，所以人们总是先发现漏点，再去测量漏量。

examples.en: A small hole in the pipe let water leak into the basement.
examples.cn: 管子上的小孔让水漏进了地下室。

examples.en: Someone leaked the report to the press before it was published.
examples.cn: 有人在报告发表前把它泄露给了媒体。

examples.en: The plumber finally found the leak behind the sink.
examples.cn: 水管工终于在水槽后面找到了漏洞。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哩可」——水从缝里「哩可」一下跑出来；leak 是漏。

root: 日耳曼语来源，一般认为与中古荷兰语 leken、古诺斯语 leka（滴落、渗漏）有关；确切词源存疑。

sensesIntro.en: The core is liquid finding a way out; the senses divide into the opening, the disclosure of secrets and the disclosed material itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是液体找到出口；义项由此分为孔洞、秘密的泄露，以及被泄露的内容本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one drop forming at a pipe joint and falling to the floor.
core.cn: 核心意象：水管接缝处凝成一滴水珠，落到地面。

branches.en: water finding a crack in an old pipe
branches.cn: 水在旧管子上找到一道裂缝

branches.en: a plumber's torch aimed behind a sink
branches.cn: 水管工的手电照向水槽后面

branches.en: a document passed to a journalist in secret
branches.cn: 一份文件被秘密交给记者

branches.en: a headline built from information that escaped
branches.cn: 用跑出来的信息做成的头条

branches.en: a wet floor under a joint that will not seal
branches.cn: 封不住的接头下方湿了一片地面

intro.en: A Germanic verb gains three English suffixes for amount, quality and person, while a homophone vegetable stays unrelated.
intro.cn: 这个日耳曼语动词加三个英语后缀，分别表示数量、性质和人物；同音的蔬菜词则并无关系。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: to let liquid or information escape
the act or amount of leaking

items.meaningCN: 形容词后缀：具有某种性质

definition_zh: 倾斜；倚靠；倾向；瘦的；精瘦的；（肉）瘦的；紧缩的
definition_en: to bend or rest against something, to tend towards a view, or to be thin, without fat or spare resources
core_image: 一个人把肩膀靠向窗框，身子斜成一条线
scene: 雨夜的车站里，旅人把肩膀靠向窗边的墙，望着外面的水汽。She leaned against the window and watched the rain.
sceneCN: 这里是「倚靠、倾斜」（第 2 个义项：把身体靠在某物上）；句意为她靠着窗看雨。可辨识画面：车站、窗边的旅人、玻璃上的水汽。

pos.zh: 瘦的；精瘦的；（肉）瘦的；紧缩的

derivatives.zh: 由 lean 加 -ing 构成，义为「倾向；倾斜」
由 lean 加 -ly 构成，义为「精瘦地」
由 lean 加 -ness 构成，义为「瘦；贫乏」
由 lean 与 to 复合，义为「单坡棚屋」

senses.title: To bend away from upright
senses.definition: to slope or bend away from a vertical position
senses.definitionCN: 偏离垂直位置而倾斜
senses.example: The old fence leans to the left.
senses.exampleCN: 那道旧篱笆向左倾斜。
senses.why: Old English hleonian meant to bend or recline, and the body's tilt is the picture the word starts from.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 hleonian 意为弯下、躺靠，身体倾斜的样子就是这个词起笔的画面。

senses.title: To rest against something
senses.definition: to put your weight on something while standing or sitting
senses.definitionCN: 站或坐时把重量放在某物上
senses.example: She leaned against the window and watched the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 她靠着窗看雨。
senses.why: If a body bends sideways, it must be held up by something, so the tilt becomes support.
senses.whyCN: 身体若向一侧弯，就得有别的东西撑住，倾斜于是变成依靠。

senses.title: To tend towards an opinion
senses.definition: to favour one choice or view more than another
senses.definitionCN: 更支持某一种选择或看法
senses.example: The committee leans towards a later start.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会倾向于晚一点开始。
senses.why: Mind leaning to one side mirrors a body leaning on a wall, so the same verb covers opinions.
senses.whyCN: 心思靠在一边，正如身体靠在墙上，同一个动词便也用来指看法。

senses.title: Thin, without much fat
senses.definition: thin in a healthy way, with little fat and firm muscle
senses.definitionCN: 瘦得健康，脂肪少而肌肉结实
senses.example: The runner had a lean, strong build.
senses.exampleCN: 那名跑步者体格精瘦有力。
senses.why: A separate Old English adjective hlǣne meant thin, and English merged it into the same spelling as the verb.
senses.whyCN: 另有一个古英语形容词 hlǣne 意为瘦，英语把它并入了与动词相同的拼写。

senses.title: Meat with little fat
senses.definition: meat that contains little fat
senses.definitionCN: 含脂肪很少的肉
senses.example: She bought lean beef for the soup.
senses.exampleCN: 她买了瘦牛肉煮汤。
senses.why: Thinness applied to meat simply means the fat has been left out, an easy extension of the bodily sense.
senses.whyCN: 「瘦」用在肉上只表示去掉了脂肪，是身体义的自然延伸。

senses.title: Short of money or supplies
senses.definition: limited in money or resources, as in lean years
senses.definitionCN: 钱财或资源有限，如艰难的年头
senses.example: The company survived several lean years.
senses.exampleCN: 公司熬过了好几个艰难的年头。
senses.why: A body without fat has nothing to spare, and a budget in the same state is called lean.
senses.whyCN: 身上没脂肪就没有余量，处于同样状态的预算也被称为 lean。

intro.en: Two Old English words, a verb of bending and an adjective of thinness, were pulled into one spelling in English.
intro.cn: 两个古英语词，一个表示弯的动词与一个表示瘦的形容词，在英语里被拉进了同一个拼写。

items.en: Hleonian meant to lean, bend or recline, and it is the source of the verb.
items.cn: hleonian 意为倾、弯、躺靠，是动词的来源。

items.en: A separate adjective hlǣne meant lean or thin, with no fat to spare.
items.cn: 另有一个形容词 hlǣne，意为瘦、没有多余脂肪。

items.en: Middle English lenen kept the verb, and the adjective was pulled into the same spelling.
items.cn: 中古英语 lenen 保留了动词，形容词也被拉进同一拼写。

items.en: The two words met in form, so one spelling now carries both bending and thinness.
items.cn: 两个词在形式上相遇，于是一个拼写同时承载「倾斜」与「瘦」。

items.en: Modern English extends the adjective to meat, budgets and hard years.
items.cn: 现代英语把形容词义扩展到肉、预算与艰难的年头。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms of this word and words that differ by a letter; the near-meaning group collects words for thinness and for tilting.
note.cn: 形近组收这个词的各种形式以及只差一个字母的词；近义组收表示瘦与倾斜的词。

entries.definition: A tendency to prefer one idea or side.
entries.definitionCN: 偏好某种想法或一方的倾向。

entries.definition: A small shelter with a sloping roof against a wall.
entries.definitionCN: 靠墙搭起、屋顶倾斜的小棚。

entries.definition: In a thin, spare way.
entries.definitionCN: 以精瘦、简省的方式。

entries.definition: A legal claim on property until a debt is paid.
entries.definitionCN: 债务清偿前对财产的法定扣押权；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To jump a long way or suddenly.
entries.definitionCN: 长距离或突然地跳。

entries.definition: Having little fat or width.
entries.definitionCN: 脂肪或厚度小的。

entries.definition: Thin in an attractive or graceful way.
entries.definitionCN: 纤细而好看的。

entries.definition: Thin, often used of a deliberate or healthy figure.
entries.definitionCN: 瘦的，常指刻意保持或健康的体形。

entries.definition: To slope or lean to one side.
entries.definitionCN: 向一侧倾斜。

normalIntro.en: A verb of bending and an adjective of thinness share one spelling, so every sense sits between a tilted body and a body with no spare fat.
normalIntro.cn: 一个表示弯的动词与一个表示瘦的形容词共用一个拼写，所以每个义项都落在「倾斜的身体」与「没有多余脂肪的身体」之间。

normal.en: Hleonian is the Old English verb for leaning, and it is the ancestor of the body sense.
normal.cn: hleonian 是古英语里表示倚靠的动词，是身体义的祖先。

normal.en: Hlǣne was a different Old English adjective for thin, so the adjective lean and the verb lean started apart.
normal.cn: hlǣne 是另一个古英语形容词，意为瘦，所以形容词 lean 与动词 lean 起初并不相干。

normal.en: Lean on and lean towards keep the picture of weight moved onto something or someone.
normal.cn: lean on 与 lean towards 保留了「把重量移到某物或某人身上」的画面。

normal.en: Lean meat is meat with the fat cut away, not meat that tilts.
normal.cn: lean meat 是去掉脂肪的肉，不是会倾斜的肉。

normal.en: Lean years are years with nothing to spare, the body sense turned into a budget.
normal.cn: lean years 是没有余量的年头，把身体义转成了预算。

abstract.en: One spelling holds two histories, so context decides whether lean is about a body or about a shortage.
abstract.cn: 一个拼写装着两段历史，所以语境决定 lean 说的是身体还是短缺。

abstract.en: Leaning on something is trust made visible: weight is handed over.
abstract.cn: 靠住某物是看得见的信任：重量被交了出去。

abstract.en: Fat is spare capacity, so a lean body and a lean budget both mean there is no margin.
abstract.cn: 脂肪是余量，所以精瘦的身体与紧缩的预算都意味着没有余地。

examples.en: She leaned against the window and watched the rain.
examples.cn: 她靠着窗看雨。

examples.en: The committee leans towards a later start.
examples.cn: 委员会倾向于晚一点开始。

examples.en: She bought lean beef for the soup.
examples.cn: 她买了瘦牛肉煮汤。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「离嗯」——身体离开竖直，靠向一边，嘴里还「嗯」了一声；记住 lean 是倾斜、倚靠。

root: 动词来自古英语 hleonian（倾靠），形容词来自古英语 hlǣne（瘦），两词在现代英语中拼写合一。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a body tilted onto support; the senses then add opinions, a thin body, lean meat and a lean budget.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一具斜靠在支撑物上的身体；义项由此加上看法、瘦削的身体、瘦肉与紧缩的预算。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shoulder pressed to a window frame, the body a straight line at an angle.
core.cn: 核心意象：肩膀抵着窗框，身体斜成一条直线。

branches.en: an old fence slowly going sideways
branches.cn: 慢慢歪向一边的旧篱笆

branches.en: a traveller's shoulder against a rainy window
branches.cn: 旅人的肩靠在下雨的窗上

branches.en: a committee raising hands for one option
branches.cn: 委员会为某个选项举手

branches.en: a runner with firm muscle and no spare fat
branches.cn: 肌肉结实、没有多余脂肪的跑者

branches.en: an empty account book in a hard year
branches.cn: 艰难年头里空空的账本

intro.en: Two Old English words, a verb of bending and an adjective of thinness, plus English endings, make up this word.
intro.cn: 两个古英语词，一个表示弯的动词与一个表示瘦的形容词，再加上英语词尾，构成了这个词。

latinIntro.en: Both the verb and the adjective are Old English, and no Latin cognate is recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 动词与形容词都来自古英语，没有记录在案的拉丁同族词。

items.meaning: a shelter leaning on a wall

definition_zh: 跳跃；跃过；骤增
definition_en: to jump suddenly, to jump over something, or to increase sharply
core_image: 一个人屈膝蓄力，整个人腾空越过一道窄沟
scene: 河岸边的鹿受到惊吓，前腿一蹬便越过灌木。The deer leaped over the low hedge.
sceneCN: 这里是「跃过」（第 2 个义项：动词，指跳过某个障碍）；句意为鹿跃过了低矮的树篱。图中可辨识物件：河岸、受惊的鹿、低矮树篱。

derivatives.zh: 由 leap 与 frog 复合，义为「跳背游戏；蛙跳式超越」
由 leap 加 -er 构成，义为「跳跃者」
由 leap 加 -ing 构成，义为「跳跃的；跃动的」

senses.title: To jump suddenly
senses.definition: to move through the air by pushing off the ground with the legs
senses.definitionCN: 用腿蹬地、身体腾空移动
senses.example: The deer leaped over the low hedge.
senses.exampleCN: 鹿跃过了低矮的树篱。
senses.why: Leap is an old Germanic verb for a springing movement, stronger and more sudden than the everyday jump.
senses.whyCN: leap 是古老的日耳曼动词，表示弹跳式的动作，比日常的 jump 更用力、更突然。

senses.title: To jump over an obstacle
senses.definition: to cross something by jumping over it
senses.definitionCN: 通过跳过去而越过某物
senses.example: He leaped the fence and ran into the field.
senses.exampleCN: 他跃过栅栏，跑进田里。
senses.why: Once the verb names the jump, the thing jumped over can become its direct object, so leap gains the sense of clearing an obstacle.
senses.whyCN: 动词既然表示跳，被跳过的东西就能作宾语，于是 leap 有了「越过障碍」的意思。

senses.title: To increase sharply
senses.definition: to rise suddenly and by a large amount
senses.definitionCN: 突然且大幅度地上升
senses.example: Profits leaped in the second quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 第二季度利润猛涨。
senses.why: A sharp rise looks like a jump on a graph, so the physical leap is borrowed for numbers that suddenly go up.
senses.whyCN: 陡升在图表上就像一次跳跃，于是身体的 leap 被借来形容数字的猛涨。

senses.title: A jump or a sharp rise
senses.definition: an act of jumping, or a sudden large increase
senses.definitionCN: 一次跳跃，或突然的大幅增长
senses.example: There was a leap in demand for electric cars.
senses.exampleCN: 电动汽车的需求出现了一次跃升。
senses.why: The noun simply names the event that the verb describes, whether in space or on a chart.
senses.whyCN: 名词只是给动词所描述的事件命名，无论在空间里还是在图表上。

intro.en: Leap is an Old English verb of springing, shared across the Germanic languages and unchanged in its central sense.
intro.cn: leap 是古英语中表示弹跳的动词，在日耳曼语族中广泛共享，核心义一直未变。

items.en: Hleapan meant to jump or spring, often with the image of pushing off the ground.
items.cn: hleapan 意为跳跃、弹起，常带有蹬地发力的画面。

items.en: The reconstructed *hlaupan is shared by German laufen, which shifted towards running.
items.cn: 重构形式 *hlaupan 为德语 laufen 所共享，后者词义转向「跑」。

items.en: Middle English lepen keeps the jump and adds the sense of jumping over something.
items.cn: 中古英语 lepen 保留跳跃义，并添上「跳过某物」的意思。

items.en: The figurative sense of a sudden rise appears in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 表示「突然上升」的比喻义在十七世纪出现。

items.en: Modern English keeps both past forms, leaped and leapt, and uses leap year for the calendar's extra day.
items.cn: 现代英语保留 leaped 与 leapt 两种过去式，并用 leap year 指日历中多出的那一天。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds and forms of leap; the near-meaning group gathers words for jumping and rising.
note.cn: 形近组收 leap 的复合词与变形；近义组收表示跳跃与上升的词。

entries.definition: A game of jumping over others, or to overtake by a jump.
entries.definitionCN: 跳背游戏；蛙跳式超越。

entries.definition: A person or animal that leaps.
entries.definitionCN: 跳跃者。

entries.definition: Moving with jumps.
entries.definitionCN: 跳跃的；跃动的。

entries.definition: The irregular past of leap.
entries.definitionCN: leap 的不规则过去式。

entries.definition: To push off and move through the air.
entries.definitionCN: 跳；跳跃。

entries.definition: A small jump on one leg or both.
entries.definitionCN: 单脚或双脚小跳。

entries.definition: A long, energetic jump.
entries.definitionCN: 大步跳跃。

entries.definition: A sudden large increase.
entries.definitionCN: 激增。

normalIntro.en: A short Germanic verb with two past forms, leap keeps its spring in space and lends it to numbers.
normalIntro.cn: 一个简短的日耳曼动词带有两种过去式，leap 把弹跳留在空间里，又借给数字。

normal.en: Leap has two past forms: leaped and leapt.
normal.cn: leap 有两种过去式：leaped 与 leapt。

normal.en: Leap over is the phrase for clearing an obstacle.
normal.cn: leap over 是表示越过障碍的搭配。

normal.en: Leap year takes its name from the extra day that makes the calendar jump.
normal.cn: leap year 得名于让日历「跳」一下的多余那一天。

normal.en: Leapfrog joins leap and frog, from a game of jumping over backs.
normal.cn: leapfrog 由 leap 与 frog 组合，来自跳过别人背部的游戏。

normal.en: Leap to conclusions means deciding without enough evidence.
normal.cn: leap to conclusions 意为没有足够证据就下结论。

abstract.en: A jump needs a firm push before it needs open air, which is why leap implies stored force.
abstract.cn: 跳跃先需要稳稳蹬地，才需要腾空，所以 leap 含着蓄力。

abstract.en: The same word describes a deer and a profit because both leave the ground suddenly.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既能描述鹿，也能描述利润，因为二者都突然离开了原来的水平。

abstract.en: In a leap, the body is briefly between two places, belonging to neither.
abstract.cn: 在跳跃中，身体短暂处在两地之间，谁也不属于。

examples.en: The deer leaped over the low hedge.
examples.cn: 鹿跃过了低矮的树篱。

examples.en: Profits leaped in the second quarter.
examples.cn: 第二季度利润猛涨。

examples.en: There was a leap in demand for electric cars.
examples.cn: 电动汽车的需求出现了一次跃升。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「力扑」——用力扑出去，就是 leap。

root: 古英语 hleapan（跳跃），与德语 laufen 同出日耳曼语族。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a springing push-off; it extends from a jump to clearing an obstacle, then to a sharp rise and the increase itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是蹬地弹起；由跳跃扩展到越过障碍，再扩展到猛涨与那次增长。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body folded at the knees, then flying clear over a narrow ditch.
core.cn: 核心意象：屈膝蓄力，整个人腾空越过一道窄沟。

branches.en: a deer lifting off the bank
branches.cn: 从河岸跃起的鹿

branches.en: a runner clearing a low fence
branches.cn: 越过矮栅栏的跑者

branches.en: a line on a graph bending upward
branches.cn: 图表上陡然上弯的线

branches.en: a single step up that changes the level
branches.cn: 改变水平的一级台阶

branches.en: the same push, one over a fence and one over last year's figure
branches.cn: 同一次发力，一次越过栅栏，一次越过去年的数字

intro.en: An Old English verb, two past endings, and a compound with frog carry the family.
intro.cn: 一个古英语动词、两种过去式词尾，以及与 frog 的复合词支撑这个词族。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 学习；学会；得知；记住；背诵
definition_en: to gain knowledge or a skill, to become aware of a fact, and to commit something to memory
core_image: 一个孩子用手指着书上的字母，一个音一个音地把它们连起来
scene: 教室里很安静，只有翻书的声音。Children learn to read by sounding out each letter.
sceneCN: 这里 learn 指「学习、学会」（第 1 个义项）；句意为孩子们通过把每个字母读出声来学会阅读。图中可辨识物件：课本、字母表、孩子的指读手势。

derivatives.zh: 由 learn 加 -er 构成，指学习者
由 learn 加 -ing 构成，指学习、学识
由 learn 加 -able 构成，指可学会的

senses.title: To gain knowledge or a skill
senses.definition: to come to know something or to be able to do something through study or practice
senses.definitionCN: 通过学习或练习而知道某事或会做某事
senses.example: Children learn to read by sounding out each letter.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们通过把每个字母读出声来学会阅读。
senses.why: The Old English verb named the act of acquiring knowledge, and its noun lār, teaching or lore, shows that learning was always something passed from one person to another.
senses.whyCN: 这个古英语动词指获取知识的行为，它的名词 lār（教导、学问）说明「学」始终是从一个人传到另一个人的事。

senses.title: To become aware of a fact
senses.definition: to be told about something or to discover a piece of information
senses.definitionCN: 被告知某事或发现某条信息
senses.example: We learned of the delay only this morning.
senses.exampleCN: 我们直到今天早上才得知延期的消息。
senses.why: Knowledge does not have to be studied: hearing a piece of news also fills the gap, so the verb extends from lessons to any newly acquired fact.
senses.whyCN: 知识不一定来自苦读：听到一条消息同样能补上空白，于是词义从课堂扩展到任何新获得的事实。

senses.title: To commit something to memory
senses.definition: to fix words or facts in the memory so that they can be repeated
senses.definitionCN: 把词句或事实记在脑中，以便复述
senses.example: The class learned the poem by heart.
senses.exampleCN: 全班把这首诗背了下来。
senses.why: Ancient learning often meant memorizing texts aloud, so the verb kept a narrower sense of storing words in the head for later recitation.
senses.whyCN: 古代的学习常意味着出声背诵文本，因此这个词保留了「把词句存进脑中以便日后复述」的窄义。

intro.en: Learn is an Old English verb of the Germanic family, and its related noun survives in the modern word lore.
intro.cn: learn 是日耳曼语族的古英语动词，它的相关名词保存在现代英语 lore 一词中。

items.en: Leornian meant to acquire knowledge, and its noun lār, teaching or lore, survives in the word lore.
items.cn: leornian 意为获取知识，其名词 lār（教导、学问）保存在 lore 一词中。

items.en: The verb belongs to a Germanic family of learning words; a link to a root meaning to track or follow a furrow is often suggested but not certain.
items.cn: 这个动词属于日耳曼语的学习词族；常有人提出它与「跟踪、沿犁沟走」的词根有关，但并不确定。

items.en: Middle English lernen kept both to learn and, in some regions, to teach, a double use that lasted for centuries.
items.cn: 中古英语 lernen 既指学，也在部分地区指教，这种两用持续了几个世纪。

items.en: The past forms learned and learnt competed, and the irregular learnt held on in British usage.
items.cn: 过去式 learned 与 learnt 竞争，不规则的 learnt 在英式用法中留存下来。

items.en: Modern English keeps learn for gaining knowledge or news, while the old teach sense survives only in dialect and in nonstandard speech.
items.cn: 现代英语的 learn 指获取知识或得知消息，古老的「教」义只在方言与非标准口语中留存。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms and derivatives of learn; the near-meaning group collects other verbs for acquiring knowledge.
note.cn: 形近组收 learn 的形式与派生词；近义组收其他表示获取知识的动词。

entries.definition: A person who is learning something.
entries.definitionCN: 正在学习某事的人。

entries.definition: Knowledge gained through study, or the process of gaining it.
entries.definitionCN: 通过学习获得的知识，或获取它的过程。

entries.definition: The British irregular past form of learn.
entries.definitionCN: learn 的英式不规则过去式。

entries.definition: To spend time reading and thinking about a subject.
entries.definitionCN: 花时间阅读并思考某个学科。

entries.definition: To fix something in the memory deliberately.
entries.definitionCN: 有意把某物记在脑中。

entries.definition: To gain a skill or possession over time.
entries.definitionCN: 逐渐获得技能或财物。

entries.definition: To find out something that was not known before.
entries.definitionCN: 发现此前不知道的事情。

normalIntro.en: The word names the act of gaining knowledge, and it has kept a plain, practical tone since Old English.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词指获取知识的行为，自中古英语以来一直保持着朴素、实用的语气。

normal.en: Old English leornian meant to gain knowledge, and its noun lār is the ancestor of lore.
normal.cn: 古英语 leornian 意为获取知识，其名词 lār 是 lore 的前身。

normal.en: Learner and learning simply add -er for the person and -ing for the activity.
normal.cn: learner 与 learning 只是分别加 -er 表示人、加 -ing 表示活动。

normal.en: Learn by heart keeps the memory sense, because the words are stored inside rather than looked up.
normal.cn: learn by heart 保留记忆义，因为词句是被存进脑中而非查出来的。

normal.en: Learn of the delay uses the news sense: knowledge arriving without study.
normal.cn: learn of the delay 用的是「得知」义：知识未经苦读就到来了。

normal.en: British English allows both learned and learnt, while American English prefers learned.
normal.cn: 英式英语过去式 learned 与 learnt 都可用，美式英语则更常用 learned。

abstract.en: A word for learning once also meant teaching, because the same knowledge moves between two people in opposite directions.
abstract.cn: 表示「学」的词曾经也指「教」，因为同一份知识在两个人之间反向流动。

abstract.en: Learning is not only reading: a rumour, a mistake and a poem all leave something behind.
abstract.cn: 学习不只是读书：一则传闻、一次错误、一首诗都会留下点什么。

abstract.en: What is learned by heart is carried without a book, which is why memory was once the main library.
abstract.cn: 背下来的东西不用书也能带着走，这就是记忆曾是主要图书馆的原因。

examples.en: Children learn to read by sounding out each letter.
examples.cn: 孩子们通过把每个字母读出声来学会阅读。

examples.en: We learned of the delay only this morning.
examples.cn: 我们直到今天早上才得知延期的消息。

examples.en: The class learned the poem by heart.
examples.cn: 全班把这首诗背了下来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「乐恩」——把学习当成一件乐事、一份恩赐；谐音记住 learn 是学习、得知。

root: 古英语 leornian（学习、获取知识），属日耳曼语词族；相关名词 lār 演变为今天的 lore（学问）。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is gaining knowledge; it widens to hearing news and narrows again to memorizing words for recitation.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是获得知识；它扩展到听到消息，又收窄为把词句背下来以便复述。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a child pointing at letters and joining their sounds one by one.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个孩子指着字母，把一个个音连起来。

branches.en: a child sounding out a first word
branches.cn: 孩子把第一个词读出声

branches.en: an apprentice watching a craftsman's hands
branches.cn: 学徒看着匠人的手

branches.en: a phone call bringing unexpected news
branches.cn: 一个电话带来意外的消息

branches.en: a poem repeated until it is fixed in the head
branches.cn: 反复念到记牢的一首诗

branches.en: a class reciting together without a book
branches.cn: 全班不看书齐声背诵

intro.en: The word is a bare Old English verb, and English builds its family with -er, -ing and -able while keeping a Germanic irregular past.
intro.cn: 这个词是光秃秃的古英语动词，英语用 -er、-ing 与 -able 扩展词族，同时保留日耳曼语的不规则过去式。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for learn; the verb and its noun belong to the Germanic family.
latinIntro.cn: learn 没有可靠的拉丁同族词，这个动词及其名词都属日耳曼语族。

definition_zh: 租约；租期；出租；承租
definition_en: a legal contract by which someone rents property; the period of such a contract; to rent something out or to take it on rent
core_image: 一沓写满条款的合同，钥匙放在最后一页上
scene: 搬进公寓之前，两个人坐在桌前逐条看合同，最后在末尾签下名字。They signed a lease for the flat before the end of the month.
sceneCN: 这里是「租约」（第 1 个义项：租赁合同）；句意是他们在月底之前为公寓签了租约。图中可辨识物件：合同、签字笔、钥匙。

derivatives.zh: 由 lease 与 hold 复合而成，义为「租赁权；租赁地产」
由 leasehold 加 -er 构成，义为「承租人；租赁权持有人」
由 lease 加 -ing 构成，义为「租赁；租赁业务」

senses.title: A legal contract for renting property
senses.definition: a legal agreement under which one party rents property from another for a period
senses.definitionCN: 一方在某一期限内向另一方租用财产的法定协议
